The food is honestly so good—you'll keep craving it because the flavors are unique. I especially love their Hawaiian Pizzatilla. It's different from the usual—slightly sweet and very smooth to eat. Their Matcha Frappe is also really good. The taste is well-balanced, not too sweet, and just right. It's also a great place if you want to build something, since it's quiet and feels like no one will disturb you. Plus, kudos to their staff—they're all very kind and welcoming. You should definitely try it. I swear, you won't regret coming here

Same goes for the matcha and the coffee drinks—nothing exceptionally good or wow-factor, but decent enough. Their cinnamon bread also leans more like a soft pandesal–briochy bun topped with cream cinnamon sauce and chocolate chips rather than the usual cinnamon roll type. What we did like is that both the palabok noodles and the sardine pasta were cooked al dente, which is always appreciated. And service-wise, the staff were warm, attentive, and quick to respond to requests. Overall, Annipie isn't somewhere I'd specifically recommend for the food itself, but it is a pleasant place to sit down for a while, rest your feet, and catch up with friends over a simple snack and coffee.

review_text: Coming in from the main Davao-Bukidnon highway, the road going to the place could be a challenge for some due one way traffic brought by on-going road widening and construction (edited Dec 2021). I guess it was not really a problem - we saw some cars, sedans and the like at the parking lot. Try to call or message first for reservations if you want to order food in advance and/or secure tables inside the restaurant. I just found out that the place is a smaller part of a 9-hectare family property. The landscape and amenities are so well-maintained. For your little ones, there is a mini playground for them to play in. The staff is friendly and accommodating. Comfort rooms are clean. Wi-fi is fast (tip: skip texting/calling your Bf or Gf, for Nature's sake- there's no signal here). You may opt to dine al fresco style, there are lots of tables at the right wing of the restaurant. We even saw some walk-in customers who were cool enough to not bother eating on a 'banig' (which the will restaurant provide) under a shade. Food is as always good especially when shared with loved ones and friends. If you're lucky on your visit, you get to sample some free native Durians as owners do their periodic harvests. Best to come in during weekdays since the weekends are expected to be packed with visitors.

review_text: We came on a monday at about 10 AM. There was a fair bit of crowd, I guess the proximity to the airport gives it an advantage. Having said that, I hope the management makes huge improvements on the food and the quality of service given that this is one of the first/last places a tourist could visit in Davao City. First and last impressions are everything. The food is so-so. Portions were small and were not prepared to standard. I ordered the breakfast platter and the sausages looked petrified and the texture was like rubber - clearly microwaved! The eggs were not cooked as per request - we had asked for the yolk to be runny. The dishes came in staggered fashion. My family was done with their meals before the breakfast platter was delivered to our table. And we probably followed up with the servers 3x, only to be waved off, ignored, and lied to. The staff in this place seem to think they owe the paying customers a favor. Left very disappointed and went to the airport annoyed instead of happy. Do better, Annipie Airport View.

review_text: We had a libre-ni-sis family lunch on Black Saturday. The sun is high but it didn't stop us in getting there. Parking is not a problem, not a single bit since Airport View compound itself has a lot of it. Albeit the heavy door to open, you get to feel cooler temperature inside. The ambience is good- with high ceiling and ample lighting. Inside, there are a lot of tables and chairs, whether it's for two or a group of ten! Should you wish to go al-fresco, no problemo as they too have sets of tables with chairs outside. Plantitas and titos, you'll love this place as potted plants abound, both in and out. Books are also part of the interior design. Food and concoctions are delicious and priced just right. I must admit, I was so full I didn't have the gastro-confidence no more for a dessert. A plateful serving of their caldereta meal had me at hello. Service water is not a thing here (for sanitary purposes), but you can order some bottled water or bring your own instead. There's also a small stall at one of its corners called Farm To Table Pantry. They sell a wide array of items from potted plants, vegetables to locally-made gourmet coffee, chocolates, perfumes, honey, tableya, skin care, beauty products, novelty items, wooven bags and more. The staff were great. The gang loved the place and so am I. Just like Arnold S. said in a movie, "I'll be back."

review_text: The place is a bit far off from the busy streets as it's located in a residential area. When we got there, there was no signage in sight to tell you that you're at the cafe. The cafe is really small inside as It can only accommodate 2 people. As for their alfresco seating, it can also only accommodate approximately five maybe six people so that's something to consider when you want to get something to drink here. In terms of their drinks, I ordered their vegan horchata since I wanted to know what horchata tastes like and as for my boyfriend, he ordered their chocolate milk. Horchata is a bit of an acquired taste, but I personally liked it. It tastes kind of like soy milk. As for the chocolate milk, I also liked it since the sweetness was balanced out by the bitter flavor of chocolate. Will try to order their coffees next time. Lastly, I recommend getting there milk cake. It's my favorite from their line of pastries! Overall, would still recommend.

review_text: @atcurbside is a delightful surprise that I got to experience during one of my rides in my hometown. The street is quite serendipitous for me as it was where I had spent most of my childhood years, and you bet this place now holds a special spot in my heart. Verdict 🍰All of their pastries are incredibly delicious, and I'm not even a cake person! I love their Mango Charlotte and Milk Cake. You'd think they're super sweet, but are actually balanced in taste and serving size. (But tbh, I could eat a whole Milk Cake by myself) ☕I've only ever tried their Spanish Cold Brew Latte (for the coffee-based drinks) and as they put it, it's a good introductory caffeinated drink for people who are new to coffee. It is quite refreshing and has enough caffeine to get me through the day. 🍵Their homemade tea is just as refreshing. Cleanses your palate well while enjoying all the cakes and quesadillas. 🍕Their beef quesadilla is not heavily marinated with powdered mixes and spices, it tastes just right. I love how each bite doesn't come with any guilt. 🍨Their affogato is a perfect cold dessert, with the nuttiness of the coffee blending well with their ice cream. I am a fan. Apart from the location and food, the owners (who run the entire place), are accommodating and friendly. You can get a sense of their pride and passion, in the work that they do, with their scrumptious food and refreshing drinks you They don't exactly have any parking space, nor bike racks, but you can park at your own risk (which isn't that risky really, lol) Location: 77 Topaz St., Marfori, Davao City They also have pop-ups at Woodridge Gate 2, Ma-a on Wednesdays and Saturdays (But best to always check their IG page for announcements, in case of changes with their schedule) P.S. I chanced upon their pop-up in December 2021, but they were already closing then, so I ended up buying their portafilter and steaming pitcher keychains instead. :D

review_text: I've been here a few times since it's one of the few 24/7 cafés in town, and the location is convenient for me when I'm in the area. The food is okay, enough to satisfy your hunger if that's the goal, but it's not something I'd go out of my way for. The same goes for the coffee. The pricing matches the portions and service. The staff is also just okay. They're not particularly friendly or polite, but at least they're not rude. The layout is a bit inconvenient as well, the pickup areas for food and coffee are separate. You can also see staff frequently passing through the main area. One thing I noticed is that they don't issue receipts, which is really odd. They also don't accept card payments. We're almost in 2026, cash feels very antediluvian, bank transfers are too much of a hassle, and QR payments aren't as convenient as a simple tap or swipe with a credit card.

The staff is also just okay. They're not particularly friendly or polite, but at least they're not rude. The layout is a bit inconvenient as well, the pickup areas for food and coffee are separate. You can also see staff frequently passing through the main area. One thing I noticed is that they don't issue receipts, which is really odd. They also don't accept card payments. We're almost in 2026, cash feels very antediluvian, bank transfers are too much of a hassle, and QR payments aren't as convenient as a simple tap or swipe with a credit card.

What made this place even more special is that I celebrated my son's 9th birthday here, upon his personal request. He really loves the food, especially the flavored wings and fries, which are perfect for kids and definitely a hit with him. It made the celebration more meaningful, knowing he truly enjoys dining here. The restaurant is clean and cozy, with a comfortable ambiance that's perfect for casual dining or special occasions. And the fact that Barok Cafe & Resto operates 24 hours is a rare find in Davao City—such a convenient option when looking for good food any time of day. I'm genuinely glad to have discovered this place. If you're looking for quality food, a kid-friendly menu, a relaxing atmosphere, and round-the-clock service, I highly recommend giving this restaurant a try.

review_text: NOT RECOMMENDED for the service and WiFi policy. The staff failed to inform me about the ONE-DEVICE RESTRICTION when providing the WiFi password, and the login page did NOT MENTION this limitation either. I only discovered the issue when I tried to transfer the connection from my phone to my laptop. When I approached the reception to clarify, I was told I'd need to purchase another drink to get a new WiFi code. Seriously? I was still on my second sip of my coffee, and you expect me to buy another cup just to use WiFi on a second device? This policy is INCONSIDERATE and poorly communicated. What's worse, there wasn't even an apology for the mishandled situation. I'm deeply disappointed by the lack of transparency and customer care. Side note: The music in the café is way too loud for any meaningful conversation or even a moment of concentration to enjoy the coffee. Overall, a frustrating experience that could have been avoided with better communication and customer service.

I hope that my feedback will encourage you to address these issues and improve the service quality for future customers. I look forward to your prompt response regarding this matter. Thank you for your attention. Sincerely, Faizel

Like they're not even familiar with their own products, embarrassing. Also, there's no bread on my order and they didn't inform ahead of time otherwise I wouldn't have ordered. The pasta was too runny and the chicken is barely there. That alone is one reason I won't recommend this place. Good ambiance though but ambiance alone is not enough to give you a good experience.

review_text: We visited Blank Space Coffee on a Sunday morning and appreciated the ample parking space. The cafe itself is quite small and intentionally dark, likely in keeping with its moody, minimalist theme. While this may appeal to those who enjoy a more introspective setting, it might feel a bit enclosed for others. We tried the dirty matcha, matcha latte V2, and a revel bar. At first sip, the matcha flavor was subtle, but it gradually developed into a more pronounced and well-balanced taste, bold yet not overpowering. I did find that I enjoyed the drinks more after asking for extra ice. The dirty matcha had a pleasant coffee kick that was smooth and didn't cause any stomach discomfort, which I personally appreciated. It struck a nice balance between being robust but not too acidic. That said, considering the portion size, I found the drinks slightly on the pricier side relative to the usual rates in Davao's coffee and matcha scene. The revel bar was a standout. It was generously sized for ₱100, moist, and not overly sweet. It felt like good value for money and complemented the drinks well. One downside during our visit was when we asked for a sales invoice and were told none could be provided. As a business, especially one that charges relatively premium prices, having proper documentation like a sales invoice is important and expected, so that was a bit of a letdown. Another thing to note is that they do not provide service water; instead, bottled water is offered at ₱20 per bottle. As for service, the two staff members on duty during our visit seemed a bit reserved and disengaged. While service was still efficient, a warmer interaction would definitely elevate the overall customer experience.

review_text: I dropped by Bluegré Coffee in Davao City today to try their Durian Caffeccino. I was curious about how it would taste, but unfortunately, the experience was a mixed bag. The service started off fine—I was greeted politely—but things went downhill when I saw the guy behind the counter picking his nose. That's an instant red flag when you're about to order food or drinks. The café itself was clean, and the atmosphere was nice. However, I was disappointed that both the upstairs area and additional seating were closed. It felt like there was limited space to sit and relax. Although sitting outside in a storm was a chilling experience for me at least. Now, about the Durian Caffeccino—I wasn't impressed. I'd rate it 3 out of 10. For ₱235 (grande), I expected something better. If you love durian, you might enjoy its strong and unique taste, but for me, it didn't work. The flavour was overwhelming in a way that didn't blend well with the coffee. So onto the ratings: Venue: 3/5 – Clean and cozy, but limited seating. Service: 3/5 – Would have been higher if not for the hygiene issue. Drink: 2/5 – Not worth the price. Would I go back? Maybe, but definitely not for the Durian Caffeccino.

That's an instant red flag when you're about to order food or drinks. The café itself was clean, and the atmosphere was nice. However, I was disappointed that both the upstairs area and additional seating were closed. It felt like there was limited space to sit and relax. Although sitting outside in a storm was a chilling experience for me at least. Now, about the Durian Caffeccino—I wasn't impressed. I'd rate it 3 out of 10. For ₱235 (grande), I expected something better. If you love durian, you might enjoy its strong and unique taste, but for me, it didn't work. The flavour was overwhelming in a way that didn't blend well with the coffee. So onto the ratings: Venue: 3/5 – Clean and cozy, but limited seating. Service: 3/5 – Would have been higher if not for the hygiene issue. Drink: 2/5 – Not worth the price. Would I go back? Maybe, but definitely not for the Durian Caffeccino.

review_text: Been here September 28, 2025 Ordered ₱170 16oz Cha Yen Tea from non coffee section. I remembered asking for the menu to be in hot but all the non coffees are in iced. Didn't mind as long as I get the sticker. I liked this drink and I think this should be the drink of the fall season. It's got that cinammon top but the subtle Thai milk tea taste compared to Asian Cow's or Baa Baa Tea's. Waited with the order beeper that will buzz loud in an already quiet 8pm stay. Yes, 8pm is also a vibe and like two to three were in here. Just pick your experience this October because they are participating in the Davao Coffee Crawl. You're going to be Journaling and if there are more people talking in there, that's up to you to tolerate that. Didn't bother with the Matcha drinks because I fear that I may taste it similar to Kisom or &Matcha. They have oatside and the Matcha container with the logo of About Life Grocer so yah pass for me. Will update when I come back. Maybe after the crawl month.

review_text: I ordered Whistle burger with mild spice; the service is well, the atmosphere feels like you're in some resort vacation. The main (mines; whistle burger with mild spice)- I love the patty in the burger isn't greasy to the point it hurts your head and somehow crispy too from it's sides! The buns are so fluffy and soft to bite on, great for those who only wanted something you can chew on. The toppings has enough spice to handle because of the jalapenos (but it's also optional to ask for spicy sauce and there's an intense option; though costly 300+). Drink (Peach pop)- there are caffeinated drinks for coffee lovers; however I choose it because I like fruity drinks. Originally ordering the Dragon one but it was sold out🥲, anyways- the fruity drinks were around 200+ pesos because of a special blend that was put in along with flower decor. Not sugary, not intense with its fruity flavor, yet it's good enough for others to drink to. I'm so thankful to getthe chance to eat at Burger Alley! 😁

review_text: Was so eager to finally make it here. Signage as well as the café wasn't as obvious (as it should be) while just driving by. Sign was still flipped to CLOSED but the civilian guard was kind enough to tell me to just go inside. One staff was still busy cleaning. So, when she faced me at the counter well, as a first-time customer I usually inquire about bestsellers (drinks and food)….. But, she just stared and S I L E N C E….. So when I asked if the Asian Spiked Coffee was delicious she immediately told me it contained alcohol which I was quick to blurt out 'Ube Espresso' (yeah, enjoyed it). When it came to the salads she kept saying Macaroni salad for some strange reason. I settled for the Waldorf (satisfying taste). I added Fresh lumpia but the Shanghai arrived instead. Telling her I couldn't eat that she sprinted to Chippens (where food orders came from). Minutes later a guy laid down the Fresh lumpia on my table (finally correct this time). Because of the P35 overage stemming from the wrong food, I added a dessert. So while this confused staff took a while to come back to the café, another lady came in. Found out she was also a staff there and we got to talking. Learned the confused staff was still three months into the job. She shot me the question, "Why Ma'am, is there a problem?" That alone I easily guessed the confused staff had prior mishaps. The latest even was the day before. Hearing problems or just not listening? I think BOTH. Same thing happened: orders weren't properly noted resulting in missed orders, wrong items sent out, etc. Well, you get the picture. With everything served, I didn't confront confused staff anymore. Telling her co-employee was enough as it was too early to be confrontational on my end. I paid the balance and she apologized (maybe after realizing her mistake). Still, I hope Management would look into this and brief said confused employee to avoid future incidents.

review_text: March 2025 — Café Basilico continues to be our reliable "go-to" in the south. They have been consistently serving us high-quality Italian-inspired dishes with generous portions and fair pricing. While there is a 6% service fee, it feels completely warranted here since the servers are attentive and proactive without being overbearing, ensuring our drinks are always full and the dining flow is seamless. We've visited twice recently, and the quality hasn't wavered. Here's a breakdown of what we've tried: First visit: Bacon Steak – ₱380 Chicken Cotoletta – ₱390 Chicken Parmigiana – ₱270 Aglio Olio – ₱270 Tiramisu Cake – ₱260 VAT + Service Charge 6% – ₱88.39 Total – ₱1,738.39 Second visit: Aglio Olio – ₱270 Chicken Cotoletta – ₱390 Beef Bourguignon – ₱390 Bolognese – ₱370 Pistachio Tiramisu – ₱360 VAT + Service Charge 6% – ₱95.36 Total – ₱1,875.36 The Chicken Cotoletta (₱390) is "goated", perfectly breaded and massive. The Bacon Steak (₱380) is another favorite for its thick, smoky cut, while the Beef Bourguignon (₱390) offers a deep, slow-cooked richness that's hard to find elsewhere in Toril. The Aglio Olio (₱270) is simple but executed perfectly with the right amount of garlic and oil. If you prefer something heartier, the Bolognese (₱370) is a solid, classic choice. For the portion sizes, these meals are easily shareable, making the value-for-money quite high. The café is highly accessible, located right along Manambulan-Tagakpan Road (the Davao-Cotabato Old Road) in Crossing Bayabas. The shared parking area fits about 12 cars max, which can get "complex" during peak weekend hours. The cozy, well-lit interior fits approximately 40 pax. The toilet is notably clean, nicely decorated, and fully PWD-accessible, which reflects their overall attention to customer comfort. Whether you're a local or just passing through the Coastal Road, this remains the best spot in Toril for a proper Italian-style meal. It's so popular now that they've even opened a Trattoria branch at SK Complex in Bajada for those who don't want to make the drive south.

review_text: Surprise! I had never expected a high standard Restaurant at this level in Toril! All of the ambience, Staff and food could easily place also in Berlin or New York. I thought it is a newly opened restaurant, just to discover it is here for more than 2 years. Even the Toilet is still at international standard (rare in the Philippines, Pinoys seems to hate clean and nice CR's...). Food serving is very fast; first salad comes after 5 Minutes... fresh lettuce! Also, the carrots and beans in our main meals are fresh, not from frozen ones. Tiramisu-Coffee was very good, no bitter background. I think it was the first coffee my wife called "good", because i make a very good coffee at home she likes, so this is a medal to the Cafe Basilico. It is for us nearly one hour drive to get there, but we are sometimes in Diegos or south, so we will come back often more on way back. Wish it would be closer to our place; it would be our favorite. The Interior has also a touch of co-working space, and they also offer Wifi, but i did not check the quality of this. Maybe the French chanson style bar music is a little bit angering, fresh beat pop songs would rather fit to the young (or at least not too old) customers. But that's my private taste, everyone else might have a different meaning about this. The Food quality indeed is beyond any critic, it is good, fresh and well prepared food made of high quality fresh ingredients.

review_text: Cafe Basilico is one of the few restaurants in Davao that strikes a good balance between ambiance and food quality. We were a group of four and spent under ₱2,000 which felt like good value considering we had salad, pizza, aglio olio, and chicken parmigiana. Everything tasted reasonably good, and the portions were satisfying. The place has a rustic charm that feels refreshing and tastefully done. It's not over-the-top or gimmicky, which I appreciate. That said, it can get quite noisy, especially when the place fills up. We also had some trouble getting the attention of the servers, partly due to the noise and partly because they weren't wearing nameplates, which made it harder to call someone over. For dessert, we originally wanted the pistachio cheesecake, but it was unavailable. We ended up trying the pistachio tiramisu, which left me a bit confused. It had the pistachio flavor, but the texture and layers were more like chiffon cake. It didn't really resemble tiramisu in taste or structure, so a different name might manage expectations better. Parking was okay but felt oddly arranged. It would help a lot if there were a security guard or staff member around to guide cars and assist in calling out vehicle owners when needed. Overall, Cafe Basilico stands out as one of the more grounded and genuinely enjoyable spots in Davao. It's not trying too hard, which in itself is a breath of fresh air. I hope they continue to improve on the little details.

review_text: We recently celebrated our 7th wedding anniversary at Cafe Basilico, and it was the perfect spot for a cozy, romantic dinner! From the moment we walked in, we felt right at home in the warm, inviting atmosphere. Let's dive into the food! -Aglio Olio: 5/5 - was hands down our favorite dish of the night. The garlic and olive oil blend was simple yet bursting with flavor, and it was cooked to absolute perfection. Every bite was a reminder of why we love this classic so much! -Truffle Pasta: 5/5 - which came in a close second. The rich, earthy truffle flavor really elevated the dish, making it a luxurious treat without being too heavy. If you're a fan of truffles, you absolutely can't miss this one! -Pomodoro Pasta: 4/5 - Honestly, it was a bit of a letdown compared to the other dishes. It wasn't bad, but it just didn't have that wow factor we were hoping for. One unexpected highlight was the toasted bread. Wow! It had this amazing smokey flavor that paired perfectly with our pasta. Seriously, don't miss out on this! -Pizza Marinara: 5/5 - Sublime! The crust was perfectly crispy, and the toppings were fresh and generous. It's the kind of pizza that makes you want to come back for more, and we definitely will. -Chicken Parmigiana: 4/5 - it was just okay. It's not bad, but it didn't stand out like the other dishes. If you're in the mood for something hearty, it'll do the trick, but I'd recommend focusing on the pasta and pizza instead. Overall, Cafe Basilico was a fantastic choice for our anniversary celebration! With standout dishes like the Aglio Olio and truffle pasta, plus that incredible toasted bread, it's a place we'll be returning to. Just remember to save room for pizza! 🍕✨

review_text: I have to say that the place is good and a bit new (less than a year). A bit noisy for a coffeeshop or cafe, more like a restaurant crowd when we get there. The interior is good for a diner/cafe so as the lighting. There is a parking outside if you have a car, but its a bit off when viewed from the outside considering the neighboring establishments or residential. The staff were a bit busy when we get there so it's understandable that things will take time but it's acceptable. Now for the food, if I am going to look at the menu, there are standard or full meal included (with meat, pizza, pasta) and the usual coffeeshop menu (coffee, cakes, sandwiches and few salads). So the good thing is you can either go there to dine for hearty meal or chill and order coffee and desserts if you like. Now the not kinda good thing if I may say is that the drinks is limited to the coffeeshop menu and does not compliment the full meal on the menu. Unless you want steak with water or coffee then its fine. No juice, soda or wine to compliment the meat or the pizza or pasta if I may say (confusing for me actually). So we ordered the afogato, a chocolate drink which i forgot the name, bianca pizza, potato wedges, italian salad, aglio olio and Bolognese pasta. For me, the afogato is good and the chocolate drink is acceptable but a bit small serving. The pizza and the toasted bread that comes with the pasta is a not so good focaccia (if its really focaccia). Their take on the aglio olio is unique for my taste but rather good while the bolognese is on the italian type base sauce. The pizza, due to the focaccia base, does not match the cheese toppings. The italian salad is also interesting. However, when they serve the food, the plating looks really nice (they deserve a pat on the back for this) and the serving size for the pasta is good for one. The potato wedges was served without any dip so good luck on that. All in all, I'd say that the place and the plating is really nice matching their pricing. Beyond that, I would say to set once expectations if your are particular with the gastronomic ride this cafe can offer.

So I felt I needed to order enough this time so I could survive the day...Lol. Anyway back to Cafe Demitasse....it is obvious to me that the Chief (s) have PASSION about food. I ordered a veggie and cheese omelet. Very delicious and filling. Fresh cheese evenly spread on top....moist but not water logged like others I have tried. Very fresh cucumber and tomato on the side. I chose toast instead of rice. The toast was eh. I would suggest maybe toast with garlic and parmesan cheese. But not a biggie. I ordered a Hawaiian pizza for later...so review later. I got a iced mocha.. yumminess galore! I'm used to a LOT of caffeine so I ordered 2 extra espresso...ok now we're talking! I also ordered a Snickers cake......delish.. Fresh...with fresh peanuts. So yes it can take a while to get your food...but it is NOT fast food...how to McDonalds or Jollibee for that. Salamat for job well done!

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: June 2025 — Cafe Gervacio's has been on my radar for a while, and it definitely lives up to the visual hype. I've been curious for three reasons: its high rating, the inviting glass-front interior that looks like a 1950s cinematic set, and the fact that it's almost always packed. After a visit to the National Museum of the Philippines – Davao (which is just a short walk away), I finally caught them at a "sweet spot" around 3:30 PM when seats were available. Almond Croissant - ₱170 is baked to perfection. The top is buttery and flaky, the middle is airy, and the base has that satisfying crunch. It's sliced and filled with a mysterious, delicious cream that elevates the whole experience without being overly sweet. It is easily one of the best croissants in the city. Iced Spanish Latte - ₱170 was a bit of a letdown. Compared to other local specialty shops or even the standard Starbucks version, this felt bland. I was looking for that distinct creamy balance of condensed milk, but it tasted a bit "thin." The ambiance is "Noir-chic" of glossy wood, low ceilings, and a polished aesthetic that feels very classy. The AC is cold and the pipe-in music adds a nice touch, though the acoustics are tricky. Because of the low ceiling, loud conversations tend to echo, so it might not be the quietest spot for deep work unless you're seated right under a speaker to drown out the noise. Service was impressive - attentive, friendly, and my food arrived in under 20 minutes. I also have to mention the comfort rooms; they are separate, aesthetic, and very well-maintained, which is a big plus for me. Outlets are scarce (I only spotted one near the entrance), so come with a full battery. For payments, they accept Cash, Credit Cards, and E-wallets. If you want a peaceful experience, aim for the mid-afternoon (3:00 PM – 4:00 PM) before the dinner crowd rushes in. I'll definitely be back to try their "proper" meals (like the Beef Tapa or Pasta).

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: We arrived after dinner (around 8 PM), hence, we didn't order any pastas or meals, only pastries/deserts and drinks. I'm rating based on: A. Quality of food and price The food itself was good, we ordered 4 pastries and all of them were delicious. The hot cappuccino and their iced sweet nostalgia was also good, although if you like your coffee sweet, you might want to consider another drink. The prices were slightly pricey for the food. Taste-wise, the chocolate roll and muffin is similar to any other pastry, but the defining feature of their pastries is the crunch, a semi-crunchy muffin and cookie was the best touch. The star of the show was the Ferrero croissant, it was flakey and buttery, and the cream was light yet adds so much flavor. 2. Service We didn't know where to order at first because waiters did not approach us (maybe because it was crowded) so when we checked the pastries up front, the owner (I assume) kindly led us back to our seats and assigned us a waiter. There were a few items that they did not add on our bill, so it got changed last minute (but it was minimal). 3. Space, Decor, and Ambiance The decor was pleasing to the eyes, it felt somewhat like a modern Japanese design mixed with hints of retro wooden furniture, and the dark blue gives off a subtle clean/luxurious feel. Ambiance was good, although towards the end there was a loud group beside our table (I would say this is beyond the control of the staff). The seats near the counter were spacious, the ones near the road, not as much.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: Cafe Gervacios is located downtown, which makes its cafe-style setup a bit unexpected in the middle of the busy area. The place has a pleasant interior and a generally relaxed atmosphere. We ordered the plant-based adobo flakes and longganisa. The adobo flakes were softer than expected. I thought it'd be crispy but it was wet and a little too salty for my taste. The longganisa was okay. Portion sizes for both were generous. What really stood out were the drinks. We had the Himalayan cafe latte and the matcha latte. Both tasted great, definitely the highlight of the meal. However, the pricing felt a bit off, as the drinks were almost as expensive as the main dishes. One thing that could use improvement is the service. There were a lot of staff present, but service was slower than expected. They also have a parking area, which is convenient, but it was muddy during our visit and took away from the overall feel of the place. Paving it would make a big difference. Overall, Cafe Gervacios has potential. The space is aesthetic and the drinks are strong.

I thought it'd be crispy but it was wet and a little too salty for my taste. The longganisa was okay. Portion sizes for both were generous. What really stood out were the drinks. We had the Himalayan cafe latte and the matcha latte. Both tasted great, definitely the highlight of the meal. However, the pricing felt a bit off, as the drinks were almost as expensive as the main dishes. One thing that could use improvement is the service. There were a lot of staff present, but service was slower than expected. They also have a parking area, which is convenient, but it was muddy during our visit and took away from the overall feel of the place. Paving it would make a big difference. Overall, Cafe Gervacios has potential. The space is aesthetic and the drinks are strong.

I asked for WiFi since it's discoverable from my device, but the wait staff just casually said it's not available (with no apology), so I cancelled my orders and decided to leave. But their whole team begged that I have to pay for my coffee since it's been made and they'll share its cost. All of them just highlighted that they will all suffer the burden of dividing the amount, but none of them sincerely apologised and gave a proactive response. So I just paid for my coffee and left. On a positive note, it's the security guard there who showed some respect and courtesy. Management should check on their guest-facing staff and train them on product knowledge, proper customer service and basic guest relations skills.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: We went there on a weekday for dinner, the place was packed with people. It was cold and clean, and has a slight smell of paint(?)/new furniture(?). A bit pricey. We tried their chocolate cheesecake and I loved it. The three cheese pizza was more tomatoey than cheesy. The beef ragu pasta was tasty albeit the pasta was slightly overcooked. We also tried their coffee: sweet nostalgia (I like this) and berry (forgot the specific name). Staff were friendly but their service was a bit unorganized. Took awhile to take our order but they were all standing near the counter, and we almost had to take the menu ourselves. But afterwards, it was flawless. All in all, food quality and service need improvement, but it's a good place to dine!

review_text: Went here after church on Mothers Day and was able to get a table without waiting. We started out with the Spanish Lattes, one hot and one iced, and both were very good. We ordered the Bacon Wrapped Sausage and Pork Adobo. Prices might be a little steep, but the food was very good and service was prompt. The cafe was full when we left and this place will be a local landmark soon for sure. Check it out for yourself!

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: Our first time to visit Cafe Gervacios, but we've heard so much about it from friends and in social media. Our curiosity brought us there after having dinner somewhere else. We were truly delighted with our late night experience at the cafe. We came less than an hour before its closing time. But it was enough for us to order coffee, tea and frappe and a few pastries. We were all happy with the service, the ambiance, and of course the food and drinks. Staff were very courteous and attentive. Even the manager/owner was very gracious and hospitable. We loved our sampling of their pastries. We tried the Ube muffin, mango sticky rice, and coffee kouign amann. Very interesting and perfectly paired with our beverages.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: Lovely cafe/restaurant, if you want a great restaurant quality experience it is one of the best places to eat at in Davao, possibly in Mindanao. You can appreciate the higher standards, the owners probably travelled the world and appreciate sharing a great culinary experience: - Food: Tasty, big variety and offering uncommon things (🇫🇷🥐, 🇩🇪🌭, 🇮🇹🍝 and homemade 🇵🇭 foods), great drinks also like the homemade cold brew coffee. - Value: Excellent (8'700 PHP for 9 people or 967 PHP per person considering that we had a huge brunch and even took food away) - Service: Welcoming, serviceable and attentive. They are well trained and serve the food quite fast. - Ambiance: Nice decors with xmas tree over xmas period, staff also hat xmas hats. Very clean and spaced tables. Well presented pastries and menu cards. Toilets were relatively clean and well equipped.

You can appreciate the higher standards, the owners probably travelled the world and appreciate sharing a great culinary experience: - Food: Tasty, big variety and offering uncommon things (🇫🇷🥐, 🇩🇪🌭, 🇮🇹🍝 and homemade 🇵🇭 foods), great drinks also like the homemade cold brew coffee. - Value: Excellent (8'700 PHP for 9 people or 967 PHP per person considering that we had a huge brunch and even took food away) - Service: Welcoming, serviceable and attentive. They are well trained and serve the food quite fast. - Ambiance: Nice decors with xmas tree over xmas period, staff also hat xmas hats. Very clean and spaced tables. Well presented pastries and menu cards. Toilets were relatively clean and well equipped.

If you're looking for a cozy place with good food, friendly service, and solid coffee, I'd definitely recommend checking it out.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: we went there this time for dessert. all their desserts were beautifully made. we ordered matcha tea eclair, chocolate eclair, ferrero, and cookies and cream frappe. matcha te eclair was my favorite. i was pleasantly surprised by the filling. very good! the chocolate eclai was ok. im just not a fan of dark chocolate. the ferrero was a surprise too. they call it ferrero croissant but it looked more like a cupcake. when i sliced it up, it was the same flaky texture of a croissant. it lacked a bit of flavor though. it had no oomph! cookies and cream frappe needed more cookies. but otherwise, i would still come back to the place. lots of food choices. the ambiance was nice and the temp cool.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: Our most favourite restaurant in Davao. In my opinion, it could pass European standards 💯. We went for brunch (9 pax) and a total bill of 8700 php with drinks, mains and desserts with 10% service charge. 👌🏻 They have private parking for their guests. Food is really delicious and uses high-quality ingredients. Pain au chocolat tastes authentic. Amazing and wide selection from pastries, artisanal coffee, appetizers, filipino and european food. The place is clean, cooled with air conditioning units, stylish interior, toilets are complete with bidet and toilet paper. It was well curated. Joshua and his team deserves recognition. Love the positive vibes they bring. 🫶🏻 Very welcoming and attentive to our needs. Glasses are filled with water whenever empty. The restaurant is only 6 months old, if they can maintain the same high standards, for sure it will be everyone's go to restaurant in Davao.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: Food is superb. There are a lot of choices, so I ordered 3 plus the oreo shake and mango cheesecake. 1. Green Goddess Quinoa Salad- my favorite. It has chicken, and the dressing (avocado celery dressing) is to die for! 2. Salmon Salpicao- wow! Now I understand why it is one of the best sellers. The sourdough is freshly made and the potato wedges… I will be back for those. 3. Longganisa on brioche topped with egg benedict (I forgot the exat name in the menu sa kalami 😋) 4. I haven't tried a mango cheesecake like this. The taste is a good combination of mango and cheese. The cheese is not overpowering. 5. Oreo Drink- super! I haven't tried their coffee yet because I chose this drink over the coffee and fresh fruit mix drinks. I have to-go boxes, perfect for breakfast the next day. The atmosphere is very nice, which is a plus. The place is a good spot for a meet-up.

review_text: Liked the vibe it's giving one time we walked pass by the place hence we visited to grab something to eat. The have a plethora of food options, some good pastries and cakes are also available. The coffee was good and apparently the use a variety of beans, some of which will cost extra. Had iced americano and the caffeine was really giving. The gerry's brownie was delectable with lots of nuts in it. The place feels like an elevated and modern take of american diner. Window blinds and warm lighting is cozy. Some seats are comfortable while some others by the window are much simpler. It is noteworthy to mention though that they charge service charge fees on your total bill

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: ~~~ I chose Cafe Gervacios for my Day 5 post-simbang gabi brekky adventure because it was the nearest to the Jacinto campus. I also love the American diner vibe of its interiors. I know cafe americano is supposed to be taken black. It's the only kind of coffee they have as a freebie for your breakfast. But, I take my coffee with sugar and cream. The brown sugar was free. Not the creamer. I had to pay for it. 😆 I ordered honey glazed chicken and waffles, and garlic rice to go with it. Pinoy po ako, kailangang may kanin. 😉🇵🇭 I loved the salad on the side, especially its dressing - balsamic vinaigrette. The salad was gone in sixty seconds. Really. The chicken fillet was fried to perfection. And that chicken dip, magnifico. 🤤 The waffles and the maple syrup were a nice meal ender. But, I didn't want it to end. 🤪 So, I ordered Ferrero to cap my breakfast off. It looked scrumptiously inviting. It was also messy to eat. 🤣 I enjoyed it. I stayed for over two hours. It was relaxing. I think I was the only customer who dined in from 6 AM to past 8AM. There were three other tables occupied by the time I left. (I fondly remember my mom. God bless her soul. She and I kind of have that 'magnet' effect when we go to restaurants. She was the the first who noticed it.) As always, I appreciate good music, which Cafe Gervacios have. ❤️🎵❤️ Pretty good taste, too. 😉 This was my third visit. The first was for dinner with high school friends. The second was for lunch - alone, as usual. Looking forward to my fourth visit. Thanks to the staff for their very warm thank you when I left, and that special "Ingat po." 🫰 I wonder where Day 6 will take me. 🤔

review_text: This is by far the friendliest establishment I have walked into in PH. From the guard at the door, to each and every staff member, the service was great. Downside, like most places, don't have a single veg/vegan item I could have with my coffee. I suggested to the person who took my order, to feedback to the chef that 1or2 vegan items would be well accepted. The Spanish latte I had was v nice and again they accommodated for me re sweetness. One of owners, Shirley, made the effort to come to my table when she heard about my dietary restrictions. She was lovely and also said she would discuss with her brother-in-law (chef) regarding introducing some items. Family run business and a 5-star experience.

review_text: Standing along the old downtown street of CM Recto, you can drive past this place during the day without even noticing it. Opens early at 9 a.m. The fair list of food offerings and a parking lot behind makes it a fitting place for small get-togethers….The Crisp Apple Salad was more on apple slices thrown in and just few lettuce leaves…The Chicken Pesto Penne with Mozzarella Pearls was just amply prepped for one person… Sweet Nostalgia Latte, I truly liked….The Creamy Spinach pizza to share tasted okay but had thick burnt edges… No need to meditate over when you are in this central part of the city… Snack items like a line of pastries in full view — have a go at their croissants… Be prepared for the spacious parking ground that's stony, uneven and can get muddy at times…

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: Finally, a luxury cafe along CM Recto! Cafe Gervacios brings a classic retro vibe infused with modern design and signature dishes. This bakery cafe offers some of the best croissants and pastries in Davao! Make sure to try their Sourdough Croissant, Basque Burnt Cheesecake, and Coffee Kouign-Amann. Pair it up with a fresh cup of coffee -- hot or iced, depending on your liking. In addition, Cafe Gervacios offers unique dishes to fill the tummy. We enjoyed Gerry's Signature Homemade Longganisa, Ham and Cheese Panini on Sourdough Bread, and Margherita Pizza. We felt comfortable inside their cozy dining area adorned with art-deco style seating and furniture. The place is also big enough for families and workmates.

place_name: Cafe Gervacios - Pastry and Coffee in Davao City
review_text: The food and the atmosphere was good. The place is a little bit crowded which is understandable since it is a newly opened café and the good qualities that I mentioned. Sadly, our order (attached photo) TOOK MORE THAN 50 minutes to serve. We were very patient about it because the place was full of customers but I noticed that the 3 groups of customers that came to the café after us were served first. That's when I approached the staff on the counter for the update of our order. We waited and it took about 8 minutes for them to approach us and ask who took our order. I was not able to know the name but I know it's a woman stationed at the counter and I mentioned my name because I know that they wrote it on the OR. They searched for our OR and found out that they misplaced it (it fell on the floor). Thankfully, they found it and confirmed our orders. They served it later on after preparing the coffee and frappe. However, they made a mistake because they served the matcha basque and eclair twice which also meant that they weren't very organized when it comes to their order system. Hopefully this will be addressed in the near future.

review_text: Ordered the Caesar salad specifically because it did not have pork. When I received the salad, it was covered in bacon pieces. I informed the waitress about this and she apologized and the kitchen remade my salad. But the bizarre thing is that after questioning the employees, it seems this is a normal practice (putting bacon on the salads). The menu clearly states what is in the salad, but it does not mention anything about pork (see picture that I've attached). Management has two ways of dealing with this: Option 1: update your menus so they are accurate. Option 2: follow the actual recipes described in the menu so people get what they order. Other than that, service was professional and excellent, food was delicious, location was convenient, and atmosphere was perfect. It would have been five stars otherwise. But because of the incorrect menu, I can only give it three stars. Also note, the restaurant is quite expensive. Don't come here if you're trying to save money. But it is high quality.

review_text: Lunched here as a group years back. And this time for early breakfast (7:30 a.m.). The Filipino/American breakfast was swift but the Continental took much longer. I expected the Hot Chocolate (tableya) to be thicker, tastier and NOT blended with milk and sugar when it reached our table. The breads were a lot as I had all four (4) selection. Four (4) spreads went with the plate as well. If you are a light breakfast eater this would definitely be very filling and would seem too much but will get you through to lunch or even a few hours after. It's imperative to try their chocolate cake in can. A hotel plus pool form part of this place's added attraction. So first-timers, you be the judge.

review_text: We have different pros and cons about a place, especially its food. So I'll start with the place. I love the place, because it's cozy and I feel completely comfortable, especially the lights and decorations are cute. The concept fit with place. They have nice and clean comfort rooms, and the pool side is nicely decorated too which is nice. The staffs are friendly, welcoming, nice and accomodating. The food is good, there's nothing extravagant with the taste, but that's okay, except for the Sisig (I forgot the price) and Seafood Laksa (299pesos). It was presentable enough for me. Food is quite pricey but it's good enough for 3-4 persons (unless all of you are voracious eaters). The cons for me is still in the food. The gravy in our Fried Chicken Steak (339pesos) was a bit cold, but the chicken is fresh and warm when served to our table. The Baby Back Ribs w/ Asian BBQ sauce (369pesos) is good and tasty, the meat is not that meaty but I think it's okay. Overall, the place and staffs are okay but there's need to improve in the food. I'll go back here in some other time to try other foods in their menu. I attached some pictures below. I forgot to take a picture for the Baby Back ribs, but there are the others that you might want to see. I also took the menu if you wanted to know how much their food, buffet, function hall and swimming pool cost.

Penne Pesto(with tuna and olives), a la pobre, and the spaghetti negra is what I've had. Egg drop sandwich also good and nice to find a chill place to have one. **Nov 2025 update** i forgot to mention that if you want a korean style egg drop sandwich, come here. The owners are very cool people too, so feel good about supporting this great local cafe.

review_text: Cafe Tavera remains a solid choice for classic Filipino seafood and comfort food near Torres Street. The Food: Definitely the highlight. Everything we ordered was delicious. We also added the Grilled Pork Liempo for some variety, and it was perfectly charred. The service is okay, though it can be a bit slow when the house is full, so patience is key. The dining area has that classic, cozy Davao ancestral home vibe, but it could use a bit of a refresh to keep up with the newer spots in the city. On-site parking is quite limited. If the small lot is full, you'll have to do roadside parking along Camus or Avanceña Streets. Just be mindful of the "No Parking" signs to avoid towing, especially since the streets are a bit narrow. Pro-Tip for Visitors: They have private air-conditioned rooms perfect for family reunions or business dinners, as well as more intimate corners for couples. Since this is a favorite for local celebrations, be sure to book in advance, as they are often packed on weekends and holidays.

review_text: We went here for lunch on a Sunday around noon and only one other customer. The little cafe was clean and inviting. We got a table and were brought menus. You can enter through the jewelry store next door and also there is a second entrance. The menu has some good choices for food and drink and we ordered a Flat White, Affogato à la Maison, Waffles and the Spanish Sardine Panini. The Flat White was full bodied and smooth and the Affogato was as you would expect, bold and creamy, and the pistachio pieces on top really accented it nicely. The sardine panini was light and flavorful with the cheese and sardines complimenting each other. The waffles were cooked perfectly and the light syrup and blueberry jam along with banana made for a special dish. A great dining experience and attentive staff get the five stars!

review_text: This cafe is proof that a beautiful space cannot make up for complete operational failure. While the decor and ambiance deserve a perfect five stars, every other aspect of our experience was a frustrating disaster. We ordered two drinks and two cakes. After waiting over 40 minutes with no update, we finally asked about our order. That's when they started to scramble. Our drinks arrived about ten minutes later, and both of them were wrong. My friend sipped her hot drink, which was fully covered, and found it was matcha. We did not order matcha. We sent them back. The cakes arrived next, and thankfully they were correct. We ate our entire dessert without our drinks. When we were done, my friend had to go to the counter to follow up yet again. After another long and unmarked wait, the correct drinks finally came. The taste was nothing special. Just okay. A few minutes later, another set of the same cakes was brought to our table. They were so disorganized they did not even know what had been served. Honestly, looking back, we should not have told them. It would have been a small compensation for their total lack of professionalism, but we are not those kinds of people. The final insult was their closing. Our correct drinks were served at 11:05 PM, five minutes after their posted closing time of 11:00 PM. We asked if we could stay to finish, since the delays were their fault and staff were still cleaning. Instead of speaking to us, they began turning the main lights on and off repeatedly. It was a rude and impatient way to treat paying customers. TLDR: Gorgeous to look at, painful to experience. The service is chaotic, the wait is absurd, and the management is clearly in over its head. Do not believe the hype or the vloggers. This cafe is not ready for customers.

review_text: When I arrived there with a friend around noon, there were a couple of stuff I wanted to take note on. One, the staff. When we arrived, they greeted us as soon as we entered, although we were the only customers there so I'm not sure if that would be consistent during peak hours. Second, the service and the food. My friend ordered the cheesy chicken, and I had the spicy hanoy chicken (I was told it was supposed to be honey but it turned out like that due to a misprint in the menu lol) and the cookies and cream frappe. It took around 20 minutes for the food to come out, which is sort of decent in my books considering this isn't a fast food restaurant. The spicy honey chicken was really good, although the rice was a bit dry and the ratio of meat to rice favored the meat more. Additionally, we had a free side dish of kimchi and egg drop soup. I couldn't eat the kimchi because of shrimp allergy but my friend finished both our shares so I'm guessing it was okay, and the egg drop soup was delicious even though I usually prefer it a bit thicker. For those who follow the Seventh Day Adventist diet (no pork, no crustaceans, fish w/o scales etc), I would recommend making sure you know what they're serving with the food since one of the side dishes we had on the plate were squid strips. Also, the food was warm when it came out. Not quite room temperature, but not exactly giving "freshly cooked". The frappe was to die for. That's all I have to say on my drink. Their garden was beautiful and clean, little to no clutter in sight. But there were pretty big dogs in a cage around the back so if you have allergies, or if you're terrified you might wanna avoid going to the corner of their outdoor dining area. They were pretty docile, though. I didn't check their bathrooms out, unfortunately, but the inside area was clean as well and didn't have any weird smells. Even the area outside smelled alright despite being beside a river and a busy road, although I'm not sure how the scent would be at night since we went there around 12 noon. Next, the prices. I'm aware inflation exists and is pretty bad, so I understood the frappe (it was a decent size dw) costing around 150+ and our food was 200+ each, but bro 50 pesos for extra rice? In summary: Do I like the place? Yes. Was the food good? Yes. Would I recommend it for outings and stuff? Maybe a one-time thing, but not enough to go back again and again. Maybe for the frappe heh. Recommend to tourists? Sure, absolutely.

I couldn't eat the kimchi because of shrimp allergy but my friend finished both our shares so I'm guessing it was okay, and the egg drop soup was delicious even though I usually prefer it a bit thicker. For those who follow the Seventh Day Adventist diet (no pork, no crustaceans, fish w/o scales etc), I would recommend making sure you know what they're serving with the food since one of the side dishes we had on the plate were squid strips. Also, the food was warm when it came out. Not quite room temperature, but not exactly giving "freshly cooked". The frappe was to die for. That's all I have to say on my drink. Their garden was beautiful and clean, little to no clutter in sight. But there were pretty big dogs in a cage around the back so if you have allergies, or if you're terrified you might wanna avoid going to the corner of their outdoor dining area. They were pretty docile, though. I didn't check their bathrooms out, unfortunately, but the inside area was clean as well and didn't have any weird smells. Even the area outside smelled alright despite being beside a river and a busy road, although I'm not sure how the scent would be at night since we went there around 12 noon. Next, the prices. I'm aware inflation exists and is pretty bad, so I understood the frappe (it was a decent size dw) costing around 150+ and our food was 200+ each, but bro 50 pesos for extra rice? In summary: Do I like the place? Yes. Was the food good? Yes. Would I recommend it for outings and stuff? Maybe a one-time thing, but not enough to go back again and again. Maybe for the frappe heh. Recommend to tourists? Sure, absolutely.
sentence: Was the food good?

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: Not my first time here, but I recently had a strong craving for their caramel pecan cheesecake and let me tell you, they still nailed it! I think they're the only one in the city that serves this, and it was just as rich, nutty, and delicious as I remembered. If I had one wish though... it would be for a bigger slice! It was sooo good but sooo tiny I could cry. 😅 Then again, maybe it's the inflation and I totally get that baking ingredients aren't cheap these days. The café has both indoor and outdoor garden seating, which is a nice option. But do note that the indoor seating is quite cramped...only two tables that are pretty close together. On the plus side, the strong coffee aroma wafting through the café was therapeutic and comforting (especially if you love coffee as much as I do). Only real downside: my cheesecake took several minutes to be served. Not a dealbreaker, but a bit of a wait for something so small, haha. Still a favorite spot for me, definitely worth the visit if you're after a cozy vibe and something sweet.

review_text: Easy to catch sight of on the way to and from Tomate Cerise. It's along the nearer but narrow path from Catalunan Grande Road. Opens at 3 p.m. on weekdays so it was just recently that I thought of dropping by. Parking space was right outside (just cross the road). As it's an outdoor seating, insects are not a surprise anymore. With the scorching heat of the sun, it does get warmer. Order took a while though (25 minutes) even though I was early and the second customer. Basic fresh vegetables for salad (cucumber/carrot sticks, tomatoes, iceberg lettuce, with light vinaigrette) and fried chicken pieces was pricey yet nothing fancy. Unsweetened iced mocha was foamy and cheaper though as well as other drinks. The owner had their own abode erected but I didn't bother to go around.

review_text: I went there twice but for dinner both times. Nice place if you want nature. They have lots of tables and chairs. There is also a pool but for your eyes only. As for the food, the first time we went, their Crispy Salmon Strips were delicious because they were crunchy and still hot, we were shocked because they were so big, good for 4-5 people. Anyway, their Quesadilla and Montecristo sandwich were also delicious (it's okay, as long as they have them). But the second time we went, I went with my parents and grandparents, the food was really tough, the rib eye steak was 2k hard. We said it was just soft, hahaha, because the waiters were the ones who insisted it was well done. Why did you even ask? Anyway, the salmon strips also tasted different from the fish. They weren't hot and crispy unlike the first time we ate them. So sad. I just took them out anyway, my wife will eat them for the lovely furbabies. The shakes are just delicious hahaha. I've only tried vanilla, matcha, and cookies n cream. Then they don't serve it to your table, help yourselves, the staff is small.. but just be careful because the food will spill because the floor is grassy and not plain… That's it, I'll still go back if there's someone to eat or just have a snack. I wish they would improve or have consistency in their food quality❤️

review_text: We've been here before, but it was quite busy at the time, so we weren't really able to enjoy the place. This time, we dropped by around 8 AM when there were only a few customers, and it made a huge difference, we got to truly appreciate the ambiance, the spacious layout, and the beautiful interiors. I also discovered a new favorite: their Vietnamese Latte — highly recommended! Along with our drinks, we ordered the Bacon 4 Cheese Sandwich, which turned out to be very generous in portion size and definitely too much for two people. We could barely finish both slices. Lol. Regarding the pricing, some say it's more expensive than Starbucks, but based on our order, we definitely got our money's worth, and then some. The barista was very patient and accommodating. It took us a while to decide, but she remained polite, offered great recommendations, and clearly explained what each blend included. We ended up going with her suggestions and they did not disappoint. Pro tip: The best time to visit is in the morning, when it's still quiet and relaxed. The worst time is late afternoon, as the place tends to get really crowded by then.

review_text: Coffee Project is a newly opened Cafe at Vista Mall in Mintal, Davao City. The ambiance is cosy, walls with artistic murals that add warmth and playfulness. It's a self service Cafe. Once you ordered and paid at the counter, a buzzer will be handed to you. You take it to your table and wait until it vibrates and flashes. This means your food is ready for pick up at the hand off counter. Coffee Project offers different kind of pasta, sandwiches, pizzas and the typical Filipino food which is fried chicken with rice. I ordered their Clubhouse Sandwich was humongous. My husband has chosen the Continental Breakfast with huge sausage (which was surprisingly delicious), bacon, fried egg, toasted bread with butter and marmalade, waffles with maple syrup. My verdict: Cosy place, reasonable price and delicious food. Highly recommended!

review_text: I've been asking my Manila friends feedback about this place. Told them we opened one in the city. And their feedback was not what I expected. "The place is just instragammable kaso way lamii!! ' But the hard headed me wanted to try kay bago bya.. Sooo, literal gi dayo namo ang lugar, We went there 2 weeks ago. Annndd... SUPER NICEEE ANG PLACE!! Aesthetic wise it's just remarkable. Other than that. I SHOULD have believed what my friends said. There were so much people when we got there. Fine masabtan kay bago man. Pricey sya for a Davao food standpoint. I would not have mind kung it would have surpassed my standards. We ordered Carbonara (so-so) , Beef tapa (😢), Creme Brumlee (so-so) , Cheese Pizza (lahi ang name sa menu- this was the only one na OK) and there Vietnamese Latte (mediocre). JESUS! Sa way pag dapig2.. Wa jud lami.. Mas lami pa ang Taps Beef Tapa jusko.. Nag mahal2 lang jud ko.. Huhuhuhu VERDICT: try it once aron ingnun naka try. Pero I won't go back again. There are so much better, more delicious and affordable restos and coffee shops in the city. Nothing spectacular.

Other customers came in and ordered their food after me without any problems. By the time I finished my meal, they still didn't have change for me. The cashier was irritated and ignoring me when I said I have to leave soon. She finally gave me my change after 30 minutes of pestering her. I do not recommend this restaurant. It seemed like she was hoping I would leave before getting my change back. It's one thing to not accept credit card, but it's another to not provide change in a timely manner.

review_text: We liked the ambiance. Although it's a little hot inside, the place is relaxing and quiet. I ordered carbonara pasta (with Alfredo sauce and bacon). I was asked if I'd like to add grilled chicken. I wanted more bacon in my pasta but it was not an option as an add on so I said yes to the grilled chicken for 60php. It was 300php total. When it was served my carbonara doesn't have even one bacon tidbit in it. There's only 5 small pieces of grilled chicken I paid for 60php as the add on. When we asked the staff about it, we were told it was either bacon or chicken. I paid for the extra though. The Alfredo sauce tasted good so we just let it go. The Angry Harry pasta was ok too. It was the quality of the 7-8 small pieces of ham they used that ruined it. The staff who delivered the order shoved the dish on the other table. Next to our table. I didn't care for it until I saw other reviews on here that say the same thing 😔 Pasta - Good portion for 1 person

review_text: I was looking for a coffee shop near our school, and chanced upon this cafè in Dacudao, which is around 700 meters away. Upon entering, the staff welcomed me with a pleasant greeting, super bait talaga to accommodate me. 💛 I ordered their CSL sea salt latte afterwards. However, I think the milk which they used had gone bad, so after more or less 3 sips, sumakit tiyan ko. 🙁 Thankfully, they were so kind to change it into a cafe latte instead, and the taste is good, 7/10 to my liking. Overall, I love the vibe and ambiance of the place, a conducive one to study or chill, kaso until 10:00 PM lang din sila, so if you're planning to study beyond 10:00, you may want to look for other 24/7 coffee shops. Thank you, Craft Coffee! 🫶

review_text: ☕ Craft Coffee Roastery – Butuan We purposely visited Craft Coffee Roastery, and although it's a bit far from Butuan city proper, it was definitely worth the trip! We enjoyed trying out their crafted coffee and tea — they offer a wide variety to explore. I personally loved the Merry Berry Tea; it felt like a little tea party since I had my own teapot to pour from! My hubby also enjoyed his freshly brewed coffee. 🍽️ What we ordered: • Bolognese Spaghetti – tasty and satisfying (10/10!) • Ham and Cheese Sandwiches – simple but flavorful • Of course, their signature craft coffee The ambiance was cozy and refreshing — perfect for anyone who appreciates quality brews and a relaxing atmosphere. ✅ Professional service and fast serving time added to the great experience. We also took home 1kg of coffee beans, which they helpfully powderized using their in-house machine. Great value for coffee lovers!

review_text: January 31, 2026. Was here last January 17, 2025. The menu was the same as last year but some in the food menu were added and removed. Either way, consistent sila. Deserved to have a break. Last time, I had the ₱95 Doppio which was two shots of strong espresso. I had to walk from here all the way to Bago Oshiro and vice versa to burn my coffee. Ventured to enter at 11pm as said in Facebook post since they are reopening but saw the recent post that they are open by 10am so we got in. Very thankful that the cafe is as good as new but I will say better from before. Felt more homey. Also would like to thank the staff and owner for allowing us to take part in the blessing of the cafe reopening. ₱165 Iced White Mocha and ₱130 Cortado are great. Both did not feel palpitating. Thanks for having this on the house. May come back soon but looking forward to the coffee trainings or cuppings that were offered previous years. Update: The Cortado is 6oz in cup, not 8oz. Correction.

review_text: I've been here quite often. They're like your friendly neighborhood cafe. There are times the place is full of noisy people, but majority of the time the cafe's ambiance is light and relaxing. At the time we went there, sockets are not free to charge your devices and they only have 2-3 sockets available. The place is giving "for catch-up vibes" only. The food and coffee is goooood! Though some snacks are a bit overpriced for its quantity/quality (for example the pizza, which I don't recommend) other than that, the rest of the food menu is okay. Overall, it's still worth it to keep coming back.

review_text: It was father's day and we decided to celebrate the event here. The main house was closed or perhaps only early reserved people were able to dine there. Thus we made it to the big tent, al fresco like set up. The price of food is acceptable since it was a buffet and it was a real taste of home. Though they only have limited options and mostly not suggested for a vegetarian. And if they are on a specific menu (like buffet) they don't do special orders as they are focused on what is available. Lots of parking, they have a huge area, but going here from the main road is a long narrow street and might confuse you as it is near to the fish port but yes you are at the right way. Since we are from downtown of Davao, I don't really recommend driving all the way here just to eat buffet but rather try their ala carte meals and drinks.

review_text: The only 24hrs Cafe in buhangin area. When I got there, there were no other customers and staffs are cleaning. I though it was close. Ambiance. Good for working or studying. even though it is on a high way you won't really hear much noise from the outside. Like other cafeś, they play music and can sometimes be loud when you're in a meeting you can tell the staffs naman to turn the volume down. Staffs. Accommodating. Given that they've been awake all night they're energetic and ready to cater and pretty helpful. Food. 150-200 coffee is not expensive given that the cafe allows you to charge your device and gives you free wifi. It is a plus that they asked me if I wanted chocolate or cinnamon on my cappuccino (I hate cafes that put chocolate instead of cinnamon on cappuccino and won't even ask you if you want chocolate on them). Cappuccino is "so so" I actually cant feel the bitterness of the roasted coffee. Nachos is Php200 which is also mid range for its price. Serving is a lot. I wasn't able to finish it so I ask for a lid cover which they gladly provide. Over all. If you just want to work or study in a different setting than your home, well this is not a bad place to do so. I can't really recommend the food since I have tried tastier food for the same price. That sakura tree in the middle is cute 🤣

review_text: My coworker suggested we have lunch at this cafe, and I was a bit skeptical since I didn't even know they served meals. When we got there, the place was clean and the staff were nice, so that was a good start. The thing that stood out the most was how pricey the meals were, especially given how small the serving portions. The Beef Strips was ₱360, it was just okay for that price, nothing special. The kamote chips were bland too, and it was only served after we followed up. Since there were no barriers in the kitchen, we even saw them start cooking it only after we asked. Also, I'm not sure if they have proper exhaust, or maybe it's just because the kitchen is open, but if you stay there long enough, the smoke or smell from the cooking will probably stick to your clothes.

review_text: Cake is commercial. Coffee was stale. Good designs tho but will definitely come back because of the convenience not the coffee. EDIT: I feel like I made a very lazy review that is ultimately unhelpful, but I'll try my best not to be that guy. Since the owner replied, here is an updated, hopefully much more detailed review. Cake is commercial. The fact that the cake was baked by your mother makes it, in my opinion, worse. Because you can't really fire your mother, or give her feedback about her cake without affecting your relationship. You might want to consider getting another supplier for your cake, because improvement for a young cafe is crucial. To be clear: the cake is okay, it's not bad. Some commercial cakes are not bad. Honestly, I thought you bought your cakes from SNR, which offers the same level of taste and consistency. But there is room for improvement, and there are so many suppliers for cakes that are better. But I guess doing something with your mom is also good, but there's that catch you have to embrace. I suppose what you can do is advertise the cake to be baked by your mother, so that it becomes more alluring and people are more likely to be forgiving. "Coffee was stale." I think stale was the incorrect word. I would say that the coffee was under-extracted. Not enough of the espesso flavor made it into the cup because of either two things: 1) the mug you used makes it very hard to measure and see where your milk levels should be. Honeslty the milk wasn't bad, it's just that the froth was too a half-inch too thick. So I would probably even consider using smaller mugs that make it easier for your barrista to see measurements, rather than stick with aesthetic mugs that ruin the coffee. 2) The machine you use is not commercial grade, which may be a problem in performing especially with high-volume orders. Unforunately I was not able to see what your machine was, so I'm not entirely sure about this, but it certainly feels and tastes that way. I would highly recommend auditing your coffee with a professional barrista so they can give you that consistency in every mug. Now I hope this review is helpful. I will definitely come back to see if there are any improvements!

review_text: A cozy little cat cafe tucked away on the second floor above a row of carinderias. During our visit, we met four adult exotic Persian cats and one kitten. The cats looked healthy and had their own enclosed litter area, although one male cat kept bothering two others, who seemed a bit stressed. I hope the cafe prioritizes neutering their cats and considers adopting rescued Puspins in the future. The cafe also has board games to borrow and pixel bricks for sale, making it a nice place to hang out. It can get quite noisy when the cafe is busy, so it may not be ideal if you're looking for a quiet workspace. We only tried the hot coffee and hotdog sandwich with fries, and both were good. It would be great to see non-dairy milk options added to the menu. My only suggestion is for the staff to be a bit stricter about how guests interact with the cats. Some visitors kept following and carrying them, so clearer guidelines on respectful handling would help ensure the cats' welfare while keeping the experience enjoyable for everyone.

review_text: Their menu is limited, which is to be expected since it's a little café. For food items there was lasagna and another dish or flavored fries. My husband and I both ordered lasagna and fries, his was plain and I got the sour cream. Personally the fries had way too much seasoning. As for the lasagna it was reheated, mine served almost lukewarm. Both my husband and I agreed lasagna was too salty, barely any meat or cheese. The staff was really nice and courteous and when picking out a cookie he did offer their best seller which was the triple chocolate. Unfortunately I'm a baker and was completely disappointed at how their cookie was much too dry, almost like a dry brownie, not much chocolate like the name suggests. The only thing I actually enjoyed was their passionfruit soda. Would we eat there again? Definitely not for the food. I would try their coffee but I doubt we'll be back.

BURGERS, are ok, good by local standards, but there's something cloying(disgustingly sweet) i taste when eating the burgers which i can't figure out. like eating cake, or cake with frosting, while having a burger, even when i asked for no sweet sauces on mine. I am not saying that tanggalin nila ang policy all I am saying is that if you second guess the validity of the id you can ask for an authorization letter, a gov't id of the pwd card owner, picture or medical notes if you like. review_text: Tried this newly opened Dunkin' branch near the airport. No issues with the food...the donuts are what you'd expect from Dunkin', consistent and okay. The place itself is also fine and aesthetic. However, the CUSTOMER SERVICE needs serious improvement. The staff were not very welcoming and had nonchalant expressions(parang ang lalaki ng problema sa buhay), which made the experience feel cold. There also seems to be confusion with the queue system. Since there are two entrances (one facing the airport and one facing Shell), customers don't know where the line starts or ends...there are no clear signages. I've actually raised this concern to the staff during two separate visits last Drcember 2025 and January 2026, but unfortunately, the response felt dismissive and unaccommodating. After this, I didn't visit again. It's a bit disappointing, especially for a newly opened branch in a high-traffic area where many travelers and tourists will pass through. Hopefully, management can address the service and organization soon.

review_text: One of the better coffee shops in Davao. It's a great alternative to the chain coffee shops as it is just walking distance from SM Lanang. I ordered a Flat White, while my friends ordered a Latte. I would've wanted the Flat White to be a bit stronger. For a third wave coffee shop, the notes of the beans are not as pronounced as I hoped it would be. I also tried the cheesecake but it was a bit underwhelming for me. The vibe of the coffee shop is warm and dim, perfect for intimate get togethers. I also hope that the baristas would be a bit friendlier, they were a bit closed off and not as warm as the coffee shop intends to be. I hope they can improve on their coffee strength and customer service.
