review_text: I really like the interior of the place. Although the lighting is dim, it adds to the personality of the cafe. It's a nice place to just chill and wait for time to pass by. Would not recommend reading a book here though just because of the lighting, but you could always sit by the window to get that natural lighting. As for the drinks, they offer a variety of choices which are not found in other cafés which was refreshing. I ordered their jeju matcha latte and it had this deep grassy taste which I liked, but it wasn't sweet so if you have a sweet tooth, you could probably ask for a packet of sugar to go with the latte. My boyfriend ordered their black vanilla which is basically just like a cold brew, but with vanilla flavoring. The vanilla was very rich combined with the cold brew which I enjoyed. Would definitely come back here.

review_text: First off, place is aesthetically pleasing. Food is okay, advantage ang menu na some options are not commonly found anywhere else. But the service, my goodness, it was sooo slow. I thought because at first kasi understaffed lang, but I went during a Sunday noon, it wasn't very crowded. But magbibigay lang ng menu para makastart na ako pili, it took about 5-10 mins trying to get the attention of the waiter (isa lang siya when I first got inside). In hindsight, that should've been my first red flag. Then, later on nung nadagdagan na ng wait staff and more customers dined in, ganun pa rin ang speed, di nagbago. Matagal nabigay ang food. Pati magbill out and magpabalot ng food to be taken home, matagal rin. From dining area, to kitchen, to cashiering, matagal talaga lahat. I will have my review again if we happen to pass by next time and I hope there will be a significant improvement.

I asked for a proper cup because, as a coffee lover, I never drink coffee or cappuccino from plastic or paper-plastic hybrid cups. But they only have plastic. It's not just bad taste, it's downright criminal for the environment. Nobody who loves coffee wants to drink it from a plastic cup. Perhaps people don't realize that paper cups are also made of 40% plastic and, like almost all disposable cups, can't be recycled. They end up in the ocean or in waste incineration plants, producing toxic fumes. With more than 60 billion disposable cups and sachets in the Philippines alone, that's the largest share of any country in the world. And the bad taste is an added bonus.

The atmosphere overall is decent. That said, I'd like to point out a few concerns. This morning, some of the staff were quite noisy, which was noticeable since many of the customers were students trying to study or work. A few even had to move seats because they couldn't focus due to the noise. I also observed that tables were not being cleared promptly. Used plates and glasses were left on tables for a while, making the place look messy and affecting the overall ambiance. Another issue I experienced was at the cashier. They kept asking for the exact amount when paying. While I understand the need for smaller bills or coins, it was frustrating because I was unable to provide the exact amount at the time. Because of this, I ended up not ordering additional food, which was disappointing. Overall, the food is good, but I hope these areas, especially staff behavior, table maintenance, and payment flexibility can be improved to enhance the customer experience.

review_text: Fourth Street Cafe has established itself as a peaceful, minimalist haven in Davao City, offering a Nordic-inspired aesthetic that feels both modern and comfortable. While it appears they've shifted their focus away from a full menu of short orders, this has only sharpened their dedication to what they do best: coffee and pastries. Their coffee truly stands out. The cafe boasts a top-tier Sanremo Cafe Racer espresso machine, a clear sign of their commitment to quality. The baristas know their craft, and it shows in every cup. A personal favorite is the Summer Innovators—a unique and delicious blend of two shots of espresso, water, crisp apple slices, and a vibrant lemon-passionfruit mixture. It's an incredibly refreshing and inventive take on a classic espresso drink, perfect for the local climate. Beyond the expertly crafted beverages, the cafe supports local coffee culture by offering a selection of locally sourced Davao beans alongside some Colombian varieties. This allows customers to not only enjoy a great cup in the moment but also take a piece of the cafe experience home. If you're looking for a quiet spot to enjoy a meticulously prepared coffee and a satisfying pastry in a beautifully designed space, Fourth Street Cafe is the place to be.

review_text: Good One Cafe and Yogurt is hard to miss with its all-pink facade. The interior is spacious, making it a nice spot to hang out. However, parking is quite limited, especially since the cafe shares the space with a gym under the same owner. It can get tight during peak hours. The cafe clearly attracts a social media crowd. During our visit, a number of content creators were filming, and the occasional camera flashes were a bit distracting. Understandable given the cafe's aesthetic, but worth noting if you're looking for a quiet hangout. The yogurt is self-serve at P0.95 per gram, with a good range of toppings. They also offer a variety of matcha drinks. Mine was decent for the price, and I liked that you can customize the sweetness level. However, it did take a while for our drinks to be served, which slightly affected the experience. Bonus points for issuing a sales invoice; something not all cafes consistently do.

review_text: The desserts at this coffee shop are fantastic, and the place is very spacious, which is a big plus. One standout feature is the alfresco area—something rare for coffee shops in Davao City. I've visited multiple times this year because I genuinely enjoy the ambiance and offerings. However, the customer service consistently leaves much to be desired, particularly with the cashier. Every single time I've been here, the cashier has been grumpy, rude, and unhelpful. For example, when I asked for a recommendation, she simply listed what was available without offering any real guidance. During another visit, I ordered a flat white, and she sarcastically remarked, "You're aware it's only one size, right?" It felt unnecessarily dismissive. Interactions with other staff haven't been much better. When I asked for an extra straw, a staff member just dropped it on the counter without a word, making it seem like they actively dislike engaging with customers. I've noticed many of the negative reviews here also mention rude staff, especially the cashier. I truly hope management addresses this issue because it's a significant drawback to an otherwise great coffee shop. Good customer service is essential, and this place could be so much better if the staff were friendlier and more accommodating.

review_text: I've been to Green Coffee Diversion, Davao City multiple times, especially on days when working from home gets a little too quiet or boring — and I have to say, they picked such a great location! The ambiance is beautiful and cozy, making it a perfect spot to relax or get some work done. That said, I do hope they consider expanding their food menu. While I enjoy their drinks and sweets, it would be nice to have more savory options like pasta or light meals. Eating sweets all the time can get a bit repetitive. Still, it's definitely one of my go-to spots in the city. Looking forward to my next visit — hopefully with some new food choices on the menu!

review_text: On October 28, my family and I decided to visit the Green Coffee Ecoland branch at around 9:30 pm. My wife, our three kids, and I were looking forward to enjoying a relaxing evening with some coffee. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be far from what we expected, largely due to a disturbing cleaning practice by the staff. At around 11:30 pm, the staff began cleaning the shop using what seemed to be a high concentration of Zonrox. Almost immediately, we were hit with a powerful, harsh odor that left us feeling uncomfortable and short of breath. I felt like I was almost suffocating from the fumes, and the smell lingered well after we left the coffee shop. Even two hours later, both my wife and I were still experiencing the effects of the fumes, which included lightheadedness and respiratory irritation. It's alarming that such a strong cleaning product was used indoors while customers were still present. Zonrox, which contains bleach, can be highly irritating if inhaled and potentially harmful, especially in enclosed spaces without adequate ventilation. The fumes can cause symptoms like coughing, sore throat, and even headaches or nausea if exposure is prolonged. For children, this could be particularly risky. Additionally, the floors became slippery from the cleaning, making it quite unsafe. At one point, I nearly slipped on the wet floor—a dangerous situation that could have resulted in injury. It was disappointing to have to leave before closing time because the smell and unsafe conditions were too overwhelming to stay any longer. To the management at Green Coffee Ecoland, I would strongly recommend reassessing the timing and methods of cleaning practices. Using such harsh chemicals while customers are present is not only uncomfortable but poses potential health risks. I hope this feedback helps improve future experiences for other patrons and that appropriate adjustments are made to ensure safety and comfort in the shop.

review_text: Honestly, they have the best cake selection in a cafe, much better than starbucks. Every cake i tasted has yet to disappoint me. I ordered their flat white and it was really good. I love the space because it's so spacious and each table mostly has an outlet which is pretty convenient if you're planning to study there as there are a lot of rooms to choose from. They have a 2nd floor area along with a basement area so you just have to take your pick. I also love the lighting of the space, it's very conducive for reading. It was around 6pm when we got there and there were only 2 barristas on the counter and both were taking turns making the drinks, slicing the cakes, and manning the cash register. Kudos to them for managing but they should add more staff to the counter to lessen the burden so that one of them could just focus with the payments of the customers.

review_text: Customer service is absolutely unacceptable. I went there in the morning. I stood there looking at what beans to try next (this is my second time). There were people in front of me. So I just waited. I stood there for a good 5 to 10 minutes waiting. I assumed the beans being ground was for the people ahead of me. I just thought they had a huge order. There piles of coffee already packed so I thought the people in front of me nearly had their order ready. So I asked if I can order. It turns out that the beans they were preparing was not for the people in front of me. It was for another order. The people in front of me still didn't have their order prepared. They saw me standing there. They could have at least had the courtesy that they had a lot of orders prior to me. So I told them I would just come back a little later. I got food and did a little shopping from the market. Then I came back about a little more than an hour later. I then asked if I could buy beans. But they were eating. They told me to come back in 30 mins. Ok, I understand that they were on break but they could have at least served me as I was only going to get one bag of grounded beans. It doesn't take 5 minutes to get up, get beans, get a plastic bag and prep the grinding machine. They can just let it run. I really want to try their other beans. But this really put me off going back. All it would have taken is engaging with costumers and informing them of the situation. Saying hello wouldn't hurt either. Not just letting them stand there. If this happened to tourists, this is not a good look. Will not recommend to my family and friends anymore.

review_text: Food alone is S tier! No wonder people kept on recommending this cafe. I ordered Kimchi Rice w/ Beef Tenderlion cubes and my friend ordered Beef Quesadilla, both were sooo good. The portion served were worth the price. We both ordered their spanish latte, by the time we ordered the beans that they were using had 80/20 ratio (which were the perfect balance of sweetness and bitterness, g lamian jud mig maayo sa ilang kape ug food diri HAHAAHAHA) Anyways for service and atmosphere, service alone was understandable since we came in the cafe with loads of people. Also salute to the staff last night (DVO had a slight earthquake) they responded well upon guiding the customers for their safety. Staff were so calm and collective. Atmosphere was okay, we came there and people were like by group (they were with their friends like more than group of 3.) It was a little bit noisy and I found the cafe more of a catching up setting with friends rather than studying. Well if you are planning to study here might as well bring noise cancelling earphones since it can get a bit noisy with the crowd. I also saw some students who were studying in the cafe last night with earphones on, highly suggest to bring a pair if you're planning to study here. Overall I would rate this cafe 4/5 for the food and service, will definitely be coming back here! Thank you so much to the staff last night. Your service and dedication are duly appreciated❤️

Me and my partner really enjoyed their pasta, we even ordered more for takeout! We also had dragon fruit cheesecake for dessert. The cheesecake is really good. You can tell they use quality ingredients, the same goes for their drinks. They are very knowledgeable of their drinks and food, clearly displaying culinary skills. I highly recommend. The place is far but it is honestly worth it. Would definitely go back here! It is truly a happy valley.

review_text: Update '25: boring. No music. Slow service. Slow kitchen. Taste reduced. There is only a shadow from the Hikaru from '23. We tried three time in a distance around 3 month. Always the same. Hikaru calls itself a "Cafe", but it is much more than this. Cafe, restaurant, Bar. Very good food from a rich menu, until now everything on stock (Do i miss "Sorry sir, it's not available"? No.). Different cold beer including imported and "my" Sm Light, Cocktails... good variety of cocktails! And they are mixed with passion and served well decorated! Also Live Music on Friday, Sat, Sunday. Sometimes outside, makes a nice bar feeling, sometimes inside, makes a Pub feeling. The new (and only?) Star on the Calinan Gastronomic night star! We only had one real good restaurant close to Calinan, 2, maybe 3 places more you can call a "restaurant" if you already experienced in good dining culture. Very nice decoration, very attentive Staff, Aircon is not too cold. We will become regular customers there. Five Stars would be the right for downtown Davao. For Calinan it should be 6*. Keep up the good work! PS: very cool: You have a Car wash beside! So while your car is cleaned, you can eat and drink while you are waiting. Most of the food and the beer is affordable (but not cheap...), cocktails & Steaks are more expensive. Quality needs price. You get a great return for your money!

It would be OK if they call it "Chicken Skin", but serving Skin only as "Crispy Chicken" is... very philippino. review_text: The café has a very cozy and inviting ambiance inside, though the exterior may not be as appealing since it's located in a downtown urban-poor area. Formerly known as Humble Coffee, this spot retains a "hole-in-the-wall" charm. I tried their Bandung Twist (non-coffee), which was okay but overly sweet for my taste. The choco cookie was good but felt overpriced given its small size. Their egg sandwich with homemade spread was average—the bread would have been better served warm. Service time was also noticeably slow; despite there being only two groups of customers, it still took quite a while for my cookie order to reach me, even though it was already displayed at the counter near my seat. On the bright side, I appreciate that their drinks are Singaporean-inspired, as the barista shared. Overall, while the drinks have character, I think they can still improve on their food menu since it feels too limited and, true to the name, a bit too humble.

review_text: November 27, 2025. Arrived around 7:40pm. Dripping water from the roof to entrance. Headed straight for MA slow bar at second floor since it closes at 8pm. Decided on ₱260 Ryori matcha but did not ask for sweetener. Sweetener is automatically served. The experience was great even the matcharista told us how to taste the drink and enjoy it. The Ryori on its own understandably needed sweetener but the oat milk is enough with it. Stayed there until 8:30pm but immediately placed the Matcha and iced milk in insulated mug. Added back water to the Matcha bowl so it's not wasted. This is my third slow bar here in Davao and will come back when it is convenient.

review_text: The owner/manager was nice, but some of the staff were not very welcoming and made it feel like customers were an inconvenience. One staff member even suggested that we go somewhere else, probably because they thought our group was too big, even though we weren't even that big of a group and there was still one available table that could accommodate us. Since the cafe itself is quite small and there were already other customers inside, maybe it already felt overwhelming for them, but I don't think that should show to customers if they actively encourage people to visit and grow their business. Since we ordered a generous amount of different food items, I understand that mistakes can happen, but several of our orders were forgotten and we had to follow up multiple times. What was disappointing was the lack of coordination among staff and the fact that no one apologized for the missed orders. I followed up politely, but one staff member responded rudely, as if it was such a hassle to prepare an order they forgot in the first place. The place is also much smaller than how it appears on social media. They don't seem fully prepared to accommodate bigger groups despite actively encouraging people to visit. Parking is very limited and only fits around two cars lang. Overall, the actual experience did not match how the cafe is presented online. Sana they can do better.

It's also pet-friendly, which makes it an even bigger plus for fur parents looking for a cozy spot to hang out.

review_text: I was finally able to give Hygge a try today on a Thursday morning around 9. Two occupied tables but still plenty of available tables and more seating available on the patio. The place was clean and I was greeted upon entering. There are some good and unique items on the menu so I ordered the iced Sweet Potato latte and a slice of the Caramel Sea Salt Cheesecake. I wasn't sure what to expect with the sweet potato latte, but it was very good with very subtle taste of sweet potato and just the right amount of cream. The cheese cake was light and also very good with the caramel and sea salt not over powering, but subtly infused in the cheese cake. Overall a very good experience for me. Free WiFi for two hours.

review_text: We usually eat dinner here with my classmates after our 9 PM class since Hygge is open 24 hours. There are five of us, and we all ordered the same meal, soy garlic chicken. One of us noticed that the chicken was still raw inside, so we checked the rest of our orders since we all had the same order, and unfortunately, all of them were undercooked as well. We informed the staff politely and they told us they would fix it within 5 minutes. However, after following up multiple times, 5 minutes turned into 10, then eventually 20 minutes. One staff member even seemed irritated and said "para di na hilaw, ma'am." When the replacement finally arrived, the chicken was extremely OVERCOOKED, so BURN and BLACKENED that it honestly looked more like beef than chicken. It was really disappointing, especially since we frequently dine here. We understand mistakes can happen, but better food quality and customer service would definitely improve the experience.

review_text: Went there at around 10pm for late dinner and to continue work bc its a 24-hr cafe BUT the place is very dirty. The tables have no wipes and there is still trash from previous customers. We were embarrassed to ask them because there seemed to be only 2 of them at the counter at that time and there were many customers. The coleslaw side is only 1 teaspoon small. Then our pasta is very watery, there is no pajuy bread unlike the photo posted here (same order) in other reviews. Then the worst part is that they ran out of wifi vouchers so we couldn't connect to their wifi so we just ate there and left. Also, the place is not conducive to studying at that time because one customer was loud because he had a vcall and he could have just minimized his voice as a courtesy to other customers but he didn't, he was busy in a debate meeting with his groupmates haha. I loved this cafe a year ago because I was studying my undergrad at 6am if I had quiz and exams at 8am in addu. Plus, some of the food was delicious at that time esp some tocino! I don't know what happened this time. Maybe they haven't maintained it? I was just disappointed. I understand that the cafe is open 24hrs but they should have maintained the cleanliness and quality of the food next time. Hoping you guys will improve next time! :)

review_text: I've actually been here a couple of times already before writing this review, and honestly I wouldn't highly recommend this coffee shop due to its slow food preparation process, where my friends and I usually have to wait for over 30 minutes for our meals (which happened earlier today). The chef then apologized profusely and offered to prepare a fresh batch. I'm genuinely amazed with their service and accountability, which is why I wanted to write this review and let everyone who plans to visit here that despite the slow service, I hope you'll still choose to visit this place. 🫶🫶

review_text: I don't usually go to Toril area, but since Indahouse has a pretty strong social media presence and lots of hype online, I decided to drop by while I was in the area. It's a bit hard to spot since the signage is small, but at least parking wasn't a problem. The place is quite small. It's literally a converted container van but it's cozy and aesthetic inside. I went on a Sunday and it was packed, which is understandable. There were around 5 to 6 staff that day, so I was surprised it took almost 50 minutes to serve just four drinks (2 matchas and 2 iced coffees). That's a long wait for just four drinks. Service really needs work. We also asked for the pudding to be packed for takeout, but it was served in a dine-in plate. It took another 10 minutes just to get it repacked. Small thing, but it adds up. The drinks themselves were a letdown. The matcha, priced at ₱250–₱295, came in a small cup that wasn't even filled to the top. Taste-wise, it wasn't anything special. The milk overpowered the matcha. There are definitely better and more reasonably priced options elsewhere in Davao. Also worth noting: they don't give receipts unless you ask, not even a simple POS slip. I really wanted to enjoy my visit, especially because of the great online presence the cafe has. But there's a noticeable gap between what's presented on social media and what customers actually experience. If you're going to build a brand with that much visibility, the in-store experience really needs to keep up.

I went on a Sunday and it was packed, which is understandable. There were around 5 to 6 staff that day, so I was surprised it took almost 50 minutes to serve just four drinks (2 matchas and 2 iced coffees). That's a long wait for just four drinks. Service really needs work. We also asked for the pudding to be packed for takeout, but it was served in a dine-in plate. It took another 10 minutes just to get it repacked. Small thing, but it adds up. The drinks themselves were a letdown. The matcha, priced at ₱250–₱295, came in a small cup that wasn't even filled to the top. Taste-wise, it wasn't anything special. The milk overpowered the matcha. There are definitely better and more reasonably priced options elsewhere in Davao. Also worth noting: they don't give receipts unless you ask, not even a simple POS slip. I really wanted to enjoy my visit, especially because of the great online presence the cafe has. But there's a noticeable gap between what's presented on social media and what customers actually experience. If you're going to build a brand with that much visibility, the in-store experience really needs to keep up.
sentence: That's a long wait for just four drinks.

If you want good matcha, this place aint it.

review_text: Indahaus feels like a hidden Japanese cabin in the middle of Davao — warm wood, thoughtful, personalised furniture, and an ambience that lets you escape the city without actually leaving it. Their matcha stands out for its clean, pure flavour, and I love that they offer different powders so you can choose exactly how you want it, whether you're in the mood for something single origin or multiblend cultivars. They also have coffee and hojicha if you feel like mixing it up. Don't miss the turon, it's my favourite thing on the menu and the perfect local twist to go with your drink. Service is warm and genuine, thanks to the friendly owners who make you feel like you're visiting an old friend's cabin rather than just another café.

review_text: Indoor Cafe is truly one of my favorite places. ❤️ It's such a cozy little spot, and you can feel the owner's passion for coffee in every single cup he makes. I also love their tea, especially when I have a cold. It's comforting and made with so much care. The owner is incredibly kind and generous. review_text: We are relatively blessed in Toril to have quite a number of coffee shops to have opened up over the years, but they are mostly freezing cold boxes with loud obnoxious music, Inherent Coffee gets the coffee shop formula right - it's chill, it's got people in there working, there IS music, not exactly to my taste(for a coffee shop) and not as background as I would like it to be, but at least it's not super obnoxious, and the selection itself nothing really offensive, top 40 radio playlist. **update** the music vibe is much improved now with chill ambient music/beats. -feb 2026 The coffee and the food was great. The coffee rivals the best other coffee shops here in Toril (there are other good places to get good coffee, but worse than awful food, as is the case in Solace, or the general disco vibe in a refrigerator ambiance, overall, for me, sucks), the food was great, it even had some garnish on it, which is something a lot of people don't pay any attention to, and the chicken katsu that I had was nice and crispy but juicy and tender inside, very good, no complaints. The only thing that I can complain about is it was still too cold inside. I walked in and I had to walk right back out to go get my jacket which I happened to have because I was riding my motorcycle. It would not hurt anybody to just keep their air temperature at 27° - no one is uncomfortable at 27°. My only other minor complaint is that if you want to sit and have a meal and if you happen to bring a laptop too, to do work, the tables are very small, and can just barely accommodate any food on them; they're like tables really meant to just have a cup of coffee on. They do have some more tables outside on their balcony which then you can also enjoy the local air temperature, and it is shaded, but then you have to breathe the smog and suffer the street noise and the heat and humidity, but the place is open until 5:00 a.m.!!!!! which is super cool, so later at night the balcony could be a nice option. The location is very good, it's near the center of Toril on a pretty big road but not a major major roadway with lots of high-speed trucks roaring by. If you want a more chill location with also great food and coffee, Cafe Sierra is still the number one spot in Toril, a more living room vibe, while Inherent Coffee seems more professional and proper coffee shop. Overall glad to have this excellent new addition in Toril which I will gladly return to as long as I have a jacket to wear, but I wish they would adjust their air conditioning to a temperature where anyone can be comfortable with the clothing that we have to wear outside (while also saving BIG money on their electric bill).

review_text: First of as a graveyard girly I'm so happy that more places are open past midnight aside from fastfood restaurants. Given that this cafe is located on the outskirts it made me so happy that they're open until 2am 🙏 Place is small but cozy. We went midnight and it's quiet, with few people working/studying. Tonkatsu is good big serving I was so full. Sandwich is what it should taste like nothing fancy big serving too. Cake is so so. Coffee. Needs improvement though 🙏 Salted Caramel Latte and Ice shaken Macchiato tasted the same for some reason. We're big on coffee and iced shaken should be stronger that normal lattes but its not the case on this one and for some reason I cannot taste the caramel which is a let down. As for my salted caramel which is not salted at all 🥲 taste like a normal latte I really think this cafe has potential though it really needs improvement. I still love that the place is cozy. Will definitely come back to try other stuff and might as well bring my work there as phone has good reception 🥹 forgot to ask if they have wifi and outlets for charging though

review_text: #reysrestaurantreview J.A.S Caffeinated There are so many things to like about Caffeinated. a. The location is perfect. Accessible but not congested. b. Interior is not spectacular but not disgusting. Boring yes (God, plastic plants must be outlawed now). Plastic Plants are simply a sign of poverty of imagination. Those who know me are aware that there are only three desserts I can tolerate: banoffee is third, blueberry cheesecake is second and creme brulee is first. I have tasted creme brulee in a Parisienne deli, in Venice and all over the country. I KNOW what is creme brûlée.So don't me. Still, this is a great cafe, so I really recommend this when you are in Davao.

sentence: Their insistence that caramelized cheese cake is Creme Brulee.

They also include a glass of water free of charge unlike other coffee shops where you have to buy bottled water which is nice. The waitress was preoccupied with her phone when I walked in, I walked up to counter and asked whether I order at counter or table. She handed me a menu and I ordered at the counter. Once I placed the order she was friendly and prompt. The drink and fries were served within 3 minutes of ordering. An older lady was taking care of another table and did a good job. Atmosphere is clean, quiet and homey. Music is light upbeat jazz. AC is very good and so is the WiFi. The bathroom is clean and has TP, unlike most other establishments. Worth the walk from SM Lanang.

review_text: I wish I could give more stars! Impeccable customer service from chat to dine, excellent food and generous serving. Hopefully soon, pizzas can take over the quesadillas because I could barely taste the cheese but I enjoyed it.

review_text: The place is pleasantly located in Coca-Cola Village in the bustling area of Matina. This charming bistro offers a serene escape with its beautiful garden-themed ambiance and warm, inviting atmosphere. The food is both delicious and affordable. Despite its low ratings, our experience at JH Garden Cafe was exceptional. The food was served promptly, and the staff was friendly and attentive. Perhaps the lack of reviews can be attributed to the fact that we visited during a less crowded time. One thing for sure though is that this place is not your typical fast-food chain where you just need to line up and have your order assembled in front of you at the counter. No, they prep your food within the required amount of time for your satisfaction so this should be a good heads up for fractious individuals not to come here. Overall, if you're looking for a peaceful place to unwind, enjoy good food, and spend quality time with loved ones, JH Garden Cafe is a highly recommended place.

The iced tea drinks were also very sweet. May eat here again if there are limited options but will not recommend.

review_text: We went to this place on a Sunday evening for dinner. The place inside (first floor) is quite small but includes very cute and aesthetic designs on the wall. Also, lots of tables are outside the establishment (and we stayed there) where they offer lots of food options!! We opted for the "Unli Wings" which has 8 flavors choices, worth 299. Though my favorite order of the night was the fruit tea!! 💖 Will definitely be back there soon just to order that again lol The staff were nice too and the waiter who accommodated us was really funny. Guess he's just trying to accommodate us well which my friends and I truly appreciate as introverted people 🥺 I was the one who recommended this place to them and I'm happy 'cause we had fun catching up!! I've always known about this place 'cause it's like a safe haven for fan girls like me to go 😆 (especially KPOP and PPOP fans). They usually organize cup sleeve events here and they're actually having a 'BINI' fan event on the upper floor when we were there. The place is within Roxas Market and it was nice to be back in this area again since it's been years since we last went here together. If you're around Roxas Avenue, this is one of the places I recommend for people to go and chill.✨

Thank you parin! 🫶

Since I had already received the meal, I had no choice but to carefully eat around the bones, which was quite inconvenient and defeated the purpose of ordering a boneless dish in the first place. review_text: We waited more than an hour for the food to be served. Their reason? They only have one person in the kitchen and is new to the job. We would understand that if they have been transparent about it but they just left us guessing when our food will be served while other customers that came later than us get served. We came here with a lot of expectations as we heard a lot of good reviews about the food, not just from online but from friend and colleagues as well. The food is good, but the service is so bad! They didn't even acknowledge their mistake. They heard us getting impatient, one of us went to the counter several times to follow up with the food but they just kept on saying 5 minutes. There's a lot of 5 minutes in an hour, imagine. Do better. Edit as reply to owner: Thank you for assuring us that you'll relay this concern to your staff, but I would like to reiterate that we indeed waited for over an hour, as our dishes were only served well after 9:50 AM. We arrived at approximately 8:40 AM, appreciated being accommodated and seated, and started ordering around 8:50 AM. So no, this was not just a case of "waiting feels longer when you're hungry." We kept track of the time, and your response feels dismissive and invalidating of our concern. What makes this even more frustrating is that the place was practically empty when we arrived, so the long wait is difficult to justify. It was also such a slap to see customers who arrived after us get served first. If there was only one kitchen staff member and they were new, shouldn't the dishes have at least been prepared and served chronologically based on when orders were placed? And frankly, are customers supposed to feel indebted to you simply because you chose to remain open despite the LGU encouraging businesses to suspend operations today? If you decide to operate, then customers should still be able to expect decent service and proper food handling, not be made to feel guilty for expecting the bare minimum. We repeatedly raised concerns about how long the food was taking, yet we were repeatedly shrugged off. When the food finally arrived, it was not even hot, which clearly suggests it had been sitting at the counter for some time before being served. No one likes being kept waiting that long for food, especially with little acknowledgment or accountability. Your service was poor, and that is the reality of our experience. Accepting feedback instead of making excuses would have gone a lot further. This also does not seem to be an isolated incident, as others have voiced similar concerns about your service. Again, do better.

It was also such a slap to see customers who arrived after us get served first. If there was only one kitchen staff member and they were new, shouldn't the dishes have at least been prepared and served chronologically based on when orders were placed? When the food finally arrived, it was not even hot, which clearly suggests it had been sitting at the counter for some time before being served. No one likes being kept waiting that long for food, especially with little acknowledgment or accountability. Your service was poor, and that is the reality of our experience. Accepting feedback instead of making excuses would have gone a lot further. This also does not seem to be an isolated incident, as others have voiced similar concerns about your service. Again, do better.

review_text: Kaos Cafe has quickly established itself as a vibrant go-to destination for anyone looking to pair a cozy atmosphere with genuinely satisfying meals. Whether you are grabbing a quick mid-day bite or settling in for a leisurely meal, the comforting portions and well-balanced seasonings make it easy to find something you will love. Of course, no cafe trip would be complete without something to drink, and Kaos Cafe pairs its savory options with an impressive beverage selection. Their specialty iced coffees and rich lattes provide the ideal caffeinated kick, rounding out the dining experience seamlessly. Thanks to its winning combination of great food, inviting ambiance, and dependable drinks, Kaos Cafe delivers an all-around dining experience that keeps locals and visitors coming back for more.

review_text: It's only my second time in Davao, but I had to make sure I returned to Karlo's Gourmet & Coffee — the very first café I visited in Davao City back in 2018! Talk about a full-circle moment. We ordered their frappes and honestly… it's as simple as it gets. Sometimes simple really hits the spot. We also got their ube cheesecake to go and WOW — it's actually really good. Creamy, flavorful, and definitely something I'd order again (and again 👀). The staff were just as warm and welcoming as I remember from my first visit years ago. It's nice when a place keeps its quality and its heart. Right beneath the café is Jack's Ridge. So after happily loading up on carbs and sugar, you can trek down (and eventually climb back up 😅) for an instant leg day. Dessert first, cardio later — balance, right? Looking forward to visiting this place for the third time soon.

review_text: April 9, 2026 Arrived 10:39am. Very hot outside and decided on Kiks. Thought of seating at the corner area but knowing that it's gonna be hot and no charging station, just next to the door. Changed to sando to on the heat then ordered. Got the off-menu ₱180 Hot Vietnamese egg coffee for dinein. If I ordered at 10:44, then I got it at 11:09. They used Vietnamese arabica as said. Was told to use the spoon to scoop the coffee at the bottom. It wasn't hot anymore but I took some pictures of it so yeah. The tasting advice was good and will consider it for other egg coffee drinks. Mixed the coffee and it felt creamy then tried placing ice in it. Preferred in hot form but kept the ice because it's hot there. Once ice melts, it smells eggy when drank from cup. I guess there's a reason why straw is provided. Next is kokobop. ₱135 Kokobop with ₱25 Ube Foam was a must because it's felt centered to the cafe. But like the egg coffee, should have gotten them in takeout form for larger portions. Last is the rocket punch and it was cheesy but great as a snack. There's water dispenser with paper cups but it's not cold. Stayed from 10:39 am to 3:30 pm. Around this time, it's not a place for studying or focusing but make use of the time once you are there or check the weather. The service was great. May try kokobop with sesame foam next time.

One of the highlights of Kingdom Cafe and Bistro is their exceptional coffee. The baristas are true artisans, meticulously crafting each cup of coffee with precision and care. Whether you're in the mood for a classic cappuccino, a velvety latte, or a rich pour-over, you can expect a delicious and perfectly brewed cup of coffee that will satisfy your taste buds and give you that much-needed caffeine boost. The menu at Kingdom Cafe and Bistro is equally impressive. They offer a range of breakfast and lunch options, as well as delectable pastries and desserts. Their food is made with fresh, high-quality ingredients, and their menu features a variety of options to cater to different dietary preferences, including vegetarian and vegan choices. One of their standout dishes is the avocado toast, which is piled high with creamy avocado, fresh veggies, and a tangy lemon dressing, making it a perfect choice for a healthy and satisfying meal. They take the time to explain the different coffee brewing methods and make recommendations based on your preferences, ensuring that you get the perfect cup of coffee to suit your taste. The service is prompt, and the staff goes above and beyond to ensure that you have a pleasant and memorable experience. In addition to their excellent coffee and food, Kingdom Cafe and Bistro also offers a cozy outdoor seating area, which is perfect for enjoying a sunny day or people-watching. Overall, Kingdom Cafe and Bistro is a hidden gem that provides an exceptional coffee shop experience. From their delicious coffee and scrumptious food to their cozy ambiance and outstanding service, it's a place where you can relax, unwind, and indulge in a truly delightful coffee shop experience. Whether you're a coffee aficionado, a foodie, or simply someone who appreciates a charming atmosphere, Kingdom Cafe and Bistro is a must-visit destination.

review_text: Took more time reaching this place. Some parking at the front and adjoining lot was a relief and at least made up for the narrow road that could push anyone to panic in no time. Everything laid on the table was good. But the Potato Bites were unnecessarily cheesy to the point it's TOO MUCH. review_text: Place was aesthetically good but the coffee and service was a let down. We arrived with a few to many people sitting at the tables, when we were done ordering that is where a lot of people started to come in also. We sat down at a table where the leftover food, plates and empty cups were still on it. The service crew didn't even clean it unless you go to the counter and tell them the area we were sitting in is not yet clean. Mind you, we were waiting for our order for almost an hour, with a dirty table. We ordered at 8:33 pm, and our orders arrived around 9:26-9:30 pm (almost an hour 😭); the ice on the matcha drinks had already melted causing the drinks to be too watery after the first sip, the seasalt caramel latte is too salty and the coconut latte tasted weird. Our friends at the other table ordered the same Coconut Latte and Seasalt Caramel and they tasted different, different from what we have ordered. We also observed the people who ordered after us got their drinks first. Overall, the place is nice and very aesthetic. Personally, I think their coffee tastes nice, the problem lies with how they handle a lot of customers at the same time, the taste is very inconsistent and the service can still be improved. Would consider going here a second time during a less busy time, maybe the experience would be different and the coffee would taste better(?)

review_text: Kopi lah Roti have been operating their business since 2007. They have free wifi and the shop offers a place that makes you feel grounded in the middle of a busy city. They have seats outside and it is not crowded. However, they don't have enough space for parking. Atmosphere: I haven't been into Singapore yet but the atmosphere of the place adorned with hanging flowers and other kinds reminded me of the Crazy Rich Asian movie. I hope that makes sense. If you visit the shop, you will also notice a portrait painting of what seemed like a regular day at the Singapore. Posters of a man preparing Kopi (the national drink of Singapore) can be seen outside and inside of the shop that reminded me the importance of the Kopitiam culture to Singapore. Food: It was my first Singaporean dining experience so I gave it 5 stars. I ordered Set B for my breakfast. It was a Teh with milk, soft boiled eggs and roti kaya toast. You can enjoy the food by dipping the kaya toast to kopi then eggs but I wanted to try something different and honestly, that was a wonderful experience for me and I really enjoyed it. Service: The service is excellent and their staffs are friendy.

review_text: I really love the industrial look of Kotetsu. The iron, wood, and concrete design feels warm and functional. I would never think of using I-beams as small shelving spaces. The artful pieces were so interesting too. While a bit on the expensive side, the coffee was delicious. I especially liked the oat Spanish latte. If you're craving for something cold then I suggest their concrete latte. It's like an affogato! Also their Matilda cake was a simple and rich chocolate based dessert that paired well with the coffees we ordered. All in all I love this coffee shop that's tucked away hidden in the deepest part of Emilia Mindanao Souvenir Center.

review_text: I've heard they serve one of the best Matcha drinks in town, and so I finally had the chance to visit them last week. Unfortunately, their Hojicha Cacao did not meet my expectations. It was, I would say, bland in taste. For Php 235, I'd say try some of their drinks instead. However, please be aware that most of their drinks here is a bit pricier than Starbucks or other third-wave coffee shops. In terms of the ambiance/vibe, the place has a brutalist/industrial interior. I just find it funny that they turned off the A/C from where I am sitting, but was gracious enough to place an electric fan instead. And oh, do not pay via credit card. The staff did not informed me that they charge additional 5% on top of your total bill so I was shocked to see I was charged a higher amount. In addition, they will not provide you an invoice UNLESS REQUESTED. By law, merchants aren't allowed to charge customers with surcharges/terminal fee for every credit card transactions. I guess they get away with it because they label the additional 5% surcharge/terminal fee as "Service Charge" when you do not get charged a "Service Charge" if you pay by cash lol. I could report them to DTI for unfair practice but I do not have time to do so. Well at least, you've been informed ahead. Pay in cash if possible. If you're planning to work/study here, they do not have a WiFi so make sure you have reliable mobile data with you. They have charging outlets though.

review_text: I've been a regular at both Kotetsu and Wood and Coffee since 2024 because they make some of the best matcha blends in Davao. But my visit yesterday (1/17/26) might make me think twice about going back to Kotetsu. We grabbed a spot at one of the long wooden tables near the bar. The baristas were as friendly as ever, and the Okumidori and other drinks were delicious. A few hours in, though, we spotted bugs crawling across the table. At first, I thought they were just big ants, but they turned out to be bed bugs. I told one of the waiters about it and asked if they could clean the table after we left, but I know it would need stronger chemicals to get rid of them. We had to check all our clothes and belongings to make sure they didn't hitch a ride home with us. I'm writing this review so the owners can fix the problem. I really hope it gets sorted out soon because Kotetsu is one of my favorite cafes in the city.

review_text: The coffee shop offers ample parking space, thanks to its location in a commercial area. The interior is visually appealing and has a unique charm. However, one thing that struck me as odd was the service charge. While I understand that the service charge culture is gradually making its way into Davao City, I don't think it's justified for a small coffee shop like this. For sit-down restaurants where service demands are higher, it makes sense, but for a casual coffee shop, it feels unnecessary.

review_text: Honest review. My go-to cafe in Davao is especially near my school (ADDU). I love Kotetsu's aesthetic and concrete design look; it feels warm and not crowded, especially at night! I've been ordering their matcha series for the past few months, and I can definitely say that it exceeded my expectations, especially their matcha banana puddings. It is hella 100/100. Their matcha tastes so good; the puddings taste so good WTHHFHF, I also love their matcha biscoff, I would rate it to 95/100 !! So obsessed with it!! However, if you're looking for food such as pasta, especially aglio olio, I ate it two times last January. I hope they can improve it since it tastes dry, yet oily. The serving is too big (for me), but it is okay, considering the price. Then I have also tried their Spanish oat latte; di ako sure sa taste since di ako coffee lover, para siyang may weird after taste na di ko ma gets ang feeling, baka lang di ko siya ma appreciate, basta para siyang may bitter yet sweet ang feeling niya. Guys, please prepare at least 500-1k budget siguro kasi medjo mahal din ang menu if ever plan niyo mag visit, I go here like every thrice a month din depende sa budget, basta i love the atmosphere, buotan sad mga people there :)

review_text: The ambiance is refreshing, it's a small cafe but the layout with that big mirror gives an illusion that the place is big. It's instagramable worthy place with nice lighting and color scheme. I ordered there L'Primo Hot Coffee which is a Spanish Latte, it has the right balance of coffee and cream. I love there coffee mug, elegant and rustic. Though I feel that the mug is a bit small for it's serving, nevertheless it gives you that luxurious touch without breaking the bank. They have free wifi and electric sockets for your phone or laptops, so it's good for studying or some office works. I went there with a full belly so I wasn't able to order there food, but would try it on my next visit. Overall, this cafe is in my Top 10 small cafe's I've visited. Update: I just had their Taco Salad & Baked Mac and it tasted great. I love their Iced Salted Caramel Latte, the taste is just right. The Americano though felt a little light, I think it's the proportion of water and espresso or something like that. Overall, the experience was great and the food was great.

review_text: The place offers a wide selection of Italian comfort food. Quattro formaggi - brick oven pizza with generous cheese toppings with toasty-chewy crust. Oil and cream - based pasta dishes - great texture and authentic flavors, but definitely not "for sharing" as claimed by their staff. Roasted chicken and Osso bucco - fall off the bones, flavorful to the last bite, and not greasy. Carrot walnut cake - the best I have tasted (and I have tasted a lot of carrot cakes!). The cream cheese frosting was not too sweet and not too thick (still melty). The walnut crumb coat provided excellent texture and toasty flavor. Gelatos - do not leave the place without sampling the Lean in New York Cheesecake flavor. Coffee americano - bold and not too acidic. Staff were not too attentive (maybe because there were many customers), but were nice enough not to judge us for our big appetite.

review_text: Lara Mia has the look, feel and taste of a Bistro that could be found in Italy or some other European country. Even perhaps in the more affluent communities in the USA like Newport Beach. But Lara Mia is instead in one of the oldest communities of Davao City. Owned by 2 sisters Lara and Marie who both studied in Europe, Lara Mia offers an ecclectic menu ranging from Italian cuisine to French pastries to Filipino traditional favorites. We sampled the gelato, we also sampled their 4 cheese pizza and their prosciutto and arugula pizza as well as their cappuccno. All, without exception, we're excellent. The bistro's decor was also well done. There simply wasn't anything to criticize.

Despite the lackluster meal, I'm still open to returning at a different time. I'll definitely skip the mains and try their famous gelato next time instead.

review_text: I was glad this place was recommended to me. I was looking for good coffee with a quiet ambiance that wasn't too far from the Ateneo de Davao campus, and Lately Coffee delivered exactly that. Finding it was a bit of an adventure, though. The entrance is just a single door along the sidewalk with a small sign that's easy to miss. Behind it is a staircase leading to a beautifully designed space with warm lighting, minimalist décor, and a charming speakeasy vibe. The coffee was excellent, and the peaceful atmosphere made it an ideal place to slow down and enjoy a cup. My only minor disappointment was that the coffee was served in a take-away paper cup instead of a ceramic mug or glass, which would have made the experience feel even more special. Still, that's a small detail. I'd gladly return to explore more of their coffee offerings and try the other cookies on their menu.

I suggest better communication with customers instead of just ignoring the wait time (and even nonchalantly cleaning the cafe before making our orders.)

review_text: Manu is a new cafe in Artiaga Street, and it's quite easy to miss because there isn't a big sign outside yet. The space itself is nice. It's modern, aesthetic, well-lit, and clean. Their coffee and matcha were good, and they offer oat milk as a substitute. They also have a small selection of finger food and pasta. I also like that they open early at 7 AM and close late at 10 PM. They don't have wifi but there are plenty of sockets around the cafe if you need to charge your devices. One downside during my visit was that there were a few flies inside the cafe. I mentioned it to the staff and they brought out a candle. It would've made the experience much better if there weren't any flies, because the place really has a lot of potential. They currently accept cash and QR payments only, and they don't have a sales invoice. Parking was a bit confusing at first. I thought it was street parking only, but apparently there's a parking lot beside the cafe. Some signage for that would help. The staff were able to assist when needed, though a bit more warmth in service would make the experience even nicer. Overall, it's a promising cafe with good drinks and a nice atmosphere. With a few small improvements, it could easily become a favorite spot in the neighborhood.

review_text: Came in to order some matchas and other snacks. For my credentials, I've been to almost every major matcha cafes in town and I frequently make my own matchas at home for the past 3 years. Their matcha was disappointing to say the least. Both the matcha cloud and matcha latte were watery, pale-looking, and flavorless with very little depth. The matcha cloud in particular had a bad aftertaste from their choice of coconut water. The gelatos were also melted even while still being stored in the chiller display. For the price they are charging, you can absolutely take your money elsewhere. Don't be fooled by some of the friends and relatives leaving 5 star reviews on here to try and mask the low ratings on this place :)

Despite these issues, the café itself is very aesthetic though the place is a bit cramped. The coffee was also good, which helped make the overall experience better. With some improvements to the food, this place has a lot of potential. Food was definitely on the pricey side.

review_text: TERRIBLE!! RUDE STAFF. NO PROPER COORDINATION. MID FOOD Don't get fooled by the TikTok videos. This is one of the worst restaurants I've ever been to. WAITED FOR 1 hour and 30 minutes for an "inyoha nalang na" table. I'm not the type to wait but since my MIL wanted to dine here, we waited. Everything was so unorganized, they didn't know where to sit us. The staff assigned by the door pointed at one of the tables and said it was ours since we were a pax of 8. We waited and waited. There was a long queue outside and they had plenty of vacant tables inside and said they were "reserved." Some of the tables remained vacant the entire 1 hour and 30 minutes of our wait. THE STAFF BY THE DOOR JUST SAID IT WAS OURS AND NOW IT'S RESERVED FOR SOMEONE ELSE? That dessert guy (see attached photo) IS SO RUDE, HE NEEDS TO UNDERGO TRAINING AGAIN. When I showed my frustration and said we waited too long and were told that was our table, he said "sige, inyo nalang na, hatag nalang nako sainyo." INGANA BA ANG TARONG NA SERBISYO? INGANA BA MUTUBAG?? WALA MAN LANG NANGAYOG PASENSYA, WALAY "MAAM, SIR"?? NAA PAY TONO NA PABALANG??? NAA PAY TINANAWAN NA MURAG SI KINSA?? TARONG BA NA?? AND AFTER ALL THAT HASSLE THE FOOD WAS MID. NOT SPECIAL. PURO PA AESTHETIC. DAGHAN KAAYOG STAFF, SIGE'G LAKAW-LAKAW, PERO DUGAY KAAYO MAKA-SERVE, DUGAY KAAYO MAKA-ABOT INIG TAWAGON. OG ANG TUBIG DIRA NA NIABOT NGA HUMANA NAMIG KAON. NEVER AGAIN.

review_text: i ate lunch here with family friends a couple days ago and it wasn't really as good as i thought it would be for several reasons. food: it's a hit or miss for the meals and some dishes are a bit pricey for the serving size. i can't speak for the pastries and coffee since i didn't try them. • baked farfalle noodles were not cooked enough so it was hard. it's serving size was also small compared to other pasta dishes and their prices. baked farfalle was only ₱569 but the plate was so small compared to the prawn linguini which was bigger and for ₱559. • prawn linguini was a bit too salty. • beef shawarma vegetable was dry and had very little beef. • breakfast pork char siu genuinely looks and tastes like tocino so i don't think ₱485 was worth it. service: the waiters seemed too busy to accommodate us properly. • a waiter just handed us the tablets but they didn't even demonstrate how to navigate and order using the tablet. • we didn't have enough utensils on our table. • we had to ask for the water AND the glass. atmosphere: parking is awful. AC didn't ventilate the place well and there wasn't enough room for the waiters to even move around properly and serve food to other people without bumping into each other. • the leather seats by the wall is like the hot spot of the restaurant because it had no AC unless that's something you'd prefer. • a lot of waiters seem to just be idle either by the back of the kitchen or around the "coffee/bar area" which makes it feel so crowded inside. • i don't know why the parking is set up to be like a box so it's super hard to get in and get out. i think diagonal parking would be better but i'm not an expert at that. again, i really can't speak for the other things in their menu, particularly the coffee and pastries but my lunch was a bit disappointing because it was pricey for the size and the quality. i think you pay more for the ambience than what the dishes are actually worth. :')

Stepping inside feels like a warm hug, from the friendly baristas, humble owners, and SUPERB coffee and waffles (now with cocktail drinks!). ☕️🧇🍸 Same as the name, they roast their own beans, from high-grade local beans to imported beans. I'm a fan of their Mt. Apo beans. It's like, if you think about "Coffee delivered in a cup of excellence", PCR would be it, and this is not an exaggeration. They aim to support the local industry and spread awareness of how we have an abundant supply of coffee beans and other products. They also supply coffee beans to a lot of coffee shops, which is superb because in case they're closed, I know which shop to go to next. They also use honey and tableya, sourced from local farms, which are both amazing. The tableya makes for a great champurrado! Verdict: ☕️My ultimate favorite and go-to drink. I've always been hesitant to match waffles with meat, but they made my palate do somersaults! Absolutely delicious! 🍸Cocktails. I've never been a boozy type of person, but, I love their Midori and Rose Fizz (not sure of the name). 🍝Mom's Spaghetti. I am quite picky with spaghettis, so this makes it in my top 3 list. It is just so tasty! But what sets this place apart from all the other cafes? It's the culture. The staff make you feel like they've known you for ages, it feels like a space safe to hang out by yourself or with a group. I've always found myself bringing my family and friends here, never heard a complaint.. yet! :D There's enough parking space for cars. Hopefully, they'll have bike racks soon. It has a lot of gristle on it (chewy part of the beef or inedible part of the beef). I partnered it with iced tea and it was refreshing (apple iced tea for only 25php). All meals are served with 2 rice and an egg. When we went there, all sandwiches are not available. It was a bad timing as well, we were waiting for a sunrise but it was chilly has an overcast day (cloudy since it's about to rain).

review_text: I won't let this night to end without letting go of the disappointment that I felt. We ordered chicken wings in two different flavors, when the order finally came, me and my girlfriend was so DISAPPOINTED with how it turned out. The chicken wings was so THIN, SMALL, and it feels like it won't even reach my stomach. I didn't expect this kind of food, I don't know if we were the only one to experience this. Hopefully, you will be able to reconsider your meals if you think that your customers won't be satisfied. Halata naman siguro sa laki pa lang ng chicken na hindi siya worth it i serve, barely may laman, halos buto nalang. I was so frustrated when I saw the serving pero just to respect kasi maraming customers that time, I didn't cause a scene nalang. Sana man lang, aware din ang in charge sa size ng chicken if justifiable ba siya i serve. We don't have photos to prove our claim kasi nga sino pa ba ang gaganahan mag take ng picture kung yun na ang nasa harapan mo, we had no choice but to eat it since sayang din naman, we were so hungry and tired to argue and complain pa. I hope you'll understand where we are coming from, we won't make this review naman if hindi kami na disappoint ng grabe. We ate sa place na yan not once but twice na, and we was also disappointed during our first dine, but nag give mi ug another try. Pero yun nga still disappointed.

review_text: As a coffee enthusiast, I'm always eager to explore new coffee shops in the city. Recently, a new coffee haven for caffeine lovers opened in the developing Davao Global Township, located along the main McArthur Matina Road. After a long day at work, I decided to check out this new Seattle's Best Coffee and experience it firsthand. The establishment is impressive with its spacious two-story building, offering a modern and bustling atmosphere with a peaceful view of the surroundings. The parking lot is also ample. A wide variety of coffee flavors are available, along with other beverages to choose from. As always, my go-to medium-sized cappuccino, which met my expectations, made my day, especially when paired with a plate of "beyond meat." The service crew was also very helpful. I mistakenly mentioned my order, and even though it had already been punched in, the crew member took the time to ask her supervisor for a correction to the billing amount. The prices are also reasonable. I spent an hour relaxing there before heading home, and I couldn't believe how many people were coming in, filling up all the available seats. It's clear that Seattle's Best Coffee is becoming a popular spot. I highly recommend this coffee shop to my friends who are looking for a great coffee experience and a new place to relax while enjoying their beverages.

review_text: Relax or work. Business or pleasure. This is the place. Plus, they open early in the morning and serve breakfast. Since it is the first operational establishment inside the Davao Global Township, it became a landmark there. Many of the runners park nearby and pass by SBC to either meet with their friends or just hang out a little bit. Bathrooms are very good and clean. All gender bathroom is on the first floor then there are more bathrooms on the second floor. Many families love to hang our here because there are two big and long tables. One on the 1st floor and another on the 2nd floor. Food is great, if you love meat and oily food. Coffee is at par with their SBX cousin. There are times that the crew are just overwhelmed specially when there are so many customers. This happens more often because it also operates a drive thru. You just have to bring patience with you when you visit. Al fresco seating are abundant and very accommodating. You can definitely enjoy the natural breeze of the warm air from the outside. Internet connection is fair. And it is free. So who are we to complain. The upholstery of chairs a classy and classic in appearance. There is a nice high ceiling and in the middle of the establishment there is a deep hall. Makes the building appear really big. The security guards are very cordial and accommodating to the guests.

review_text: It was my first time ever at this place and I can say that it wasn't pleasing at all. The waiting time for our order was very long. We ordered at 6:55PM. I had high hopes for the food to be good, especially after the long wait, but the food that we received was cold and was nothing special to say the least. By the time we had the food, our drinks were already watered down by the melted ice and was not that great. The establishment itself is pretty good overall but it seems like wasted potential. Also, regardless of the amount of food you order, you have to pick it up yourself at the counter. The food portions are worth it for the price but not the taste. You can definitely find better food for the same price or less. Not really somewhere I would visit again.

review_text: I've always loved Seattle's Best and never had any issues with it. I was such a fan that I even emailed Seattle's Best Philippines to suggest opening a branch in Davao, and they responded positively, saying they'd look into it. Imagine my excitement when I found out that not one but two branches were opening in the city! When the Matina branch opened, I waited three weeks before visiting, eager to finally enjoy my favorite Javanilla Classic drink. However, my excitement was quickly dashed when I was told they didn't have ice cream for the drink. I decided to let it slide, understanding that they were still adjusting to new protocols and operations. Despite that, I kept coming back, even trying the drive-thru, but the service remained slow. A drive-thru, which is supposed to be quicker, made us wait 20 minutes for our order. I voiced my concerns once or twice, but it seemed like nothing changed. Months later, on the first day of 2025, I found myself waiting over 30 minutes in line just to place my order. When it was finally my turn, I was informed they could only serve iced drinks, meaning my Javanilla Shake was unavailable again. On top of that, I couldn't order food because the kitchen was backed up, with wait times exceeding 40 minutes. Having waited so long in line, I felt forced to settle for whatever was available. Now, after more than an hour, our drinks still haven't been served. This branch has been nothing but a disappointment, leaving me deeply frustrated and disheartened.

review_text: June 2026 – Seattle's Best Coffee is located near the entrance road leading to Davao Global Township's City Center. I have been here on several occasions, and the shop's issues have been consistent since its opening: a lack of cleanliness, and a shortage of front-desk personnel and additional POS terminals. Imagine having a long queue of customers only to be greeted by a single active register and one attending staff member, while the rest of the crew remains in the back. Cleanliness is not consistently maintained; the service crew is rarely seen clearing or wiping tables after customers leave, and the restroom is also quite dirty. Furthermore, order preparation is inconsistent. For instance, when ordering three drinks, you would expect to be given a matching number of spoons, forks, or straws, along with enough tissue to share. On the plus side, there are varied seating options available across the ground floor, the second floor, and the front alfresco area. Because it is located within the DGT development, parking is easy and readily available. However, because it sits in such an open area, mobile internet connection can also be inconsistent.

review_text: Opened its gate by 2 p.m. one weekday. The subtly run-down look of exterior walls added more to its allure. Tiramisu foam blend and the Seasalt cream tasted fine. Place was too hot as sun's rays streamed through the glass. Second time around cafe was on time (1 p.m.). The Almond latte and Lychee yakult was just unimpressively regular in taste. Some unavailable beverages that day too. Another was the food they unusually start serving later at 3:30. For some odd reason only hot beverages are allowed for carryout. Staff attitude wasn't even impressive to begin with during both visits. Just imagine what the mood of the next shift would be…Well, I tried and that's the last.

review_text: We visited your store last night because it was recommended by a friend of my husband one of your workers. We saw your shop and the ambiance is very comfy we love the ambiance But I was disappointed because of the staff and my husband ordered some of your café drinks. One of the drinks I noticed is the cappuccino, which is not standard po nia I don't know if my wrong Ok lang sana, so I went to the cashier and asked the barista if the cappuccino didn't have chocolate powder. They said there was none, but if I wanted it I could add it but there was an additional charge. Which is, I don't know what standard cappuccino is. Literally just make milk foam then pour the coffee on top, then mix it and it's like a café latte. My husband chatted with his friend and explained our experience. Then your barista said that customers don't like cocoa powder on top because it's bitter, I don't know what is the exact standard of the cold cappuccino but based on my experience at barista abroad we put chocolate powder to balance the bitterness and sweetness while sipping the coffee. We understand that not all customers like cocoa powder, but hopefully they don't do it all because customers have different preferences and one thing missing is the customer service with a genuine smile 😊 Btw only I will rate your mango yacult 9/10. We have our own small coffee shop, and we love to explore other cafés to learn and get some ideas to apply in our coffee shop. We came all the way from Kidapawan just to visit your shop, so we were a little disappointed with the experience, especially with the barista who served us. We visited around 8:42 PM. We hope this feedback helps po 🙏🏻 our coffee shop MK ROLLINGS FLAVOR CAFE

review_text: Tucked inside the bustling Gaisano Mall Davao is a charming little Starbucks branch that, while modest in size, more than makes up for it with its warm and inviting vibe. Whether you're looking for a quick caffeine fix, a place to catch up on emails, or simply somewhere to unwind, this cozy café is worth checking out. From the moment you walk in, the ambiance pulls you in — soft lighting, calm energy, and a mix of seating options that cater to both solo visitors and small groups. It's a compact space, sure, but it doesn't feel cramped. The layout makes smart use of what's available, and the stylish island counter adds a modern, functional flair. For digital nomads or anyone needing to charge up, there are power outlets available, though you might need to do a little hunting to find them. Just a heads-up for persons with disabilities (PWDs): the tight layout might make navigation a bit of a challenge. Now, here's a funny little moment — the barista didn't quite catch my name when I ordered, and instead of asking again, they just made one up. So there I was, on the little corner at the back of the island counter, sipping my Caramel Macchiato and eating my Danish Cinnamon Bread as Niel. Who's Niel? Who knows? That little Starbucks trick is having a comeback, I guess. Another pleasant surprise? The restroom. Clean, well-maintained, and clearly not an afterthought — always a welcome bonus in any café setting. All in all, Starbucks Gaisano Mall Davao is a great little hideaway amidst the mall chaos. It's not the biggest or flashiest branch, but it nails the basics: comfort, good coffee, and a peaceful spot to pause your day — even if you leave with a new name.

review_text: This Starbucks branch offers a warm, dependable experience that feels both familiar and thoughtfully run. The space is clean, well-lit, and comfortable whether you are working, meeting friends, studying, or just killing time between errands. The baristas are polite, organized, and impressively efficient even during busy periods, and they manage the crowd with calm professionalism rather than stress or attitude. I especially appreciated how they prioritized my order in the queue when I mentioned that my Grab was arriving in less than five minutes; that small act of consideration genuinely saved me stress and showed real customer awareness. The drinks were consistently well made — smooth lattes, properly balanced iced beverages, and reliable flavor every time, with customization handled without hesitation. However, on a regular day, this branch is usually a great place to hang out with friends. Just be prepared for the crowd if you're visiting during peak hours cause it can get very busy and crazy. Also, avoid seating near the glass wall from mid day to early afternoon cause the weather can get really hot.

review_text: Starbucks in SM Lanang offers a refreshing break from the typical mall-based cafe experience, primarily due to its standout location. Positioned as an "island platform" within the sprawling mall, it creates a distinct, open-air feel that sets it apart from other branches. The generous seating, both indoors and out, provides ample space for solo work or group meetups, making it a comfortable spot to linger and enjoy your coffee. The cafe's offerings are what you would expect from a Starbucks—a consistent and reliable menu of beverages and pastries that align with the brand's global standards. While the location and ambiance are unique to this branch, the food and drink options are a familiar comfort for any Starbucks enthusiast. However, a notable point for anyone planning an early visit is the discrepancy in operating hours. While online listings, including Google Maps, may indicate a general opening time of 8:00 AM, the on-site staff, as experienced firsthand, confirm a different schedule. It's a bit disappointing to be shooed away, but it's an important detail to be aware of to avoid an early morning letdown. It seems this specific branch operates on a 9:00 AM schedule, aligning with the general mall hours rather than the standard Starbucks time. This is a small but crucial piece of information for anyone who relies on those early hours for their caffeine fix. Ultimately, this Starbucks is a great spot for its ambiance and location, perfect for a mid-shopping break or a relaxed meet-up. Just be sure to double-check their actual opening hours before you go!

One thing I do hope they add soon is support for the international Starbucks app. It would be very convenient for travelers or customers like me who use the US Starbucks app to tap, pay, and earn or use rewards instead of being limited only to the local Philippine app. Overall, a good Starbucks branch with good service, decent parking depending on the gate situation, and the usual consistent Starbucks experience.

This experience has left me frustrated and concerned about the lack of attention to customers with allergy needs. While Grab, the third-party delivery company, refunded the amount I paid for the item, this incident is a serious reminder to take allergies into account more carefully. The situation regarding food allergies, especially in my case, can be life-threatening, and it's crucial that all parties involved—Starbucks, Grab, and others—take these concerns seriously moving forward.

As for the overall vibe, it strikes a nice balance between lively and relaxed. There's enough energy in the room to keep you from zoning out, but it's not so noisy that you can't focus. All in all, I'd say this is a reliable place if you're looking for somewhere to study, work, or simply have an easy meetup with friends.

The interiors are nice, most especially the floor which has a different design. You can also have a view of outside - the convention center's patio with some plants and trees which is nice. The place is quite big but can get really crowded, especially on Friday nights. They could add more chairs and tables for "outside seating" if doable. Perhaps, inside too - since I noticed that there's much space vs. the lay-out for the tables/chairs. Just a thought. Would definitely be back in this place!

review_text: April 2026 — I visited around 2:00 PM after grabbing lunch at Nanyang nearby. This is the second Starbucks branch in the SM City Davao complex, located on the first level of the SM Expansion Wing (the other being the newly renovated Annex branch). The aesthetic is a beautiful take on elevated Filipino design, featuring cushioned seats, wooden tables, ample space, warm lighting, and minimalist wall decor. However, despite the inviting ambiance, nearly every spot was taken by people on laptops with notebooks, pens, and bags sprawled across the tables. I noticed a row of cushioned seats on the right where only a few people were sitting, yet the surrounding empty seats were completely covered in their personal belongings. By 3:00 PM, which is peak coffee hour, a queue had formed with nowhere for new customers to sit. It's frustrating to see tables meant for 4 to 5 people occupied by only two, with extra chairs rendered unusable because they are being used as luggage racks. I even had to ask a guy if I could use a chair he was using as a footrest. While the service was fast, only one cashier was on duty and no printed receipts were available. Starbucks is known for its "Third Place" policy, but I feel it occasionally cultivates a culture of taking up too much space without regard for others. In Bisaya, we call this behavior "dalok" which means an unwillingness to share, and in this case, chairs and tables in a communal shop.
