review_text: STASH Coffee is located on the second floor of a business building. Might be hard to see from the street, but it is there just as Google map shows. The place was clean, nice ambiance, plenty of available seating and even a couple of tables with chairs in a little nook next to the elevator. I was greeted by the friendly staff and was brought a menu. After looking over the menu I decided on the Black Sparkle (iced espresso and tonic water) and the Big Breakfast. The Big Breakfast was really big so it is well named. The sausage was well cooked, juicy, and just enough spice so it didn't need any hot sauce. The eggs paired well with the sausage, mushrooms and the bread. Great combo! The coffee was bold and smooth and overall very refreshing. A hot coffee might have been better with the Big Breakfast, but I'm not complaining. Over a great experience! The free WiFi was good and the CR was clean.

review_text: A friend recommended Stash Coffee, stating it was the best in the city, and she was right. The lemonade and iced tea were exceptional—refreshing with a hint of mint, and served like cocktails, all for a reasonable price of 110 pesos each. They were indeed a perfect remedy for the city's humidity. I also enjoyed their beef tapa. As a balikbayan on holiday, I missed the classic Filipino breakfast, and their beef tapa offered a perfect balance of sweetness, saltiness, and garlic flavour. I appreciated that it was paired with garlic-fried rice and a sunny-side-up egg; it brought back fond memories of home. One area where Stash Coffee could improve is its Pulled Pork Sandwich. While it was flavorful, it was served in large slices, which made it difficult to chew. They might consider shredding the pork to make it easier for customers to enjoy.

review_text: I'm glad I had chanced upon this coffee spot when I visited Davao. Its closed to USEP and Victoria Plaza. They have a parking space and manned by security guards which is a plus for safety. The cafe had decent space and still have lovely Christmas decors. I love the industrial feel and theme of this coffee place. I asked for reco and the barista recommended their house special, Spanish Latte. I expected it to be sweet but surprsingly wasn't which is good. I prefer less sugar and this latte was perfect. It had subtle taste of mocha and still strong for the espresso kick. I finish it after 5 pages of reading my book. I was the only customer in the place, and I want to stay but longer to finish what I'm reading and got another coffee, this time cafe americano. I can tell they have single origin coffee and was right when the barista told me that beand was from Burundi which is notably for clean, delicate and fruity flavor. I did totally enjoy every sip of it. Both staffs are friendly and I say well trained esp the lady barista. She knows her craft well. Too bad, they don't have any food offerings when I visit since it was still after NY. Another reason for a next visit.

review_text: Stash is owned by the same people behind Purge Coffee Roasters in Tulip Dr. Both brew the best coffees in the city. Here are my personal favorites: 1. Mocha Lava 2. Honey Lemon Tea 3. Spanish Latte 4. Matcha Latte Mocha Lava ☕️+🍨 became an instant favorite of mine from Stash and Purge. Espresso shot on ice then topped with chocolate ice cream. I usually prefer bitter-sweet coffee and the mocha lava, in particular, perfectly matched my taste. White Peak is also my favorite but for takeaway. Stash and Purge sell it in bottles. It's milky, but the caffeine remains strong. From experience, the buzz lasts for 5-6 hours. It's a must-buy. Honey Lemon Tea 🍯🍋 is always a good idea when I feel like skipping coffee. Mint leaves are added; thus, it gives off a cooling sensation even when the drink is hot. Sweet. A little kick of sourness. Minty. It's a therapeutic drink for me. They also have cakes and pastries on display although subject to availability. I had a slice of carrot cake on my very first visit and it was delightful. Pesto pasta from Stash totally clicked with my tastebuds. The pesto sauce and chicken meat were generous. Di tinipid. Sakto lang ang dami ng parmesan cheese. Overall, it was delicious and flavorful. The staffs were fun to look at. They all got along together. Moreover, they were courteous and well-trained. From time to time, they checked on the customers. Stash has a peaceful ambiance. Their regular customers usually come to order coffee and do work. Some hold small business meetings. Others spend their time to study. But Stash is also family-friendly. They got high chairs for toddlers. Stash has good parking space and tidy comfort room. Plus, dili boring ilang menu especially their drinks. They have other nice options for those who want to skip or don't drink coffee. 🙌🏻⭐️

The place is just cramped, there isn't really a lot of comfortable sitting areas since their place is small, but it's okay for me since I wanted my drink to-go and I didn't really intend to sit and spend time at the place. Overall, if you're coming over for a matcha or hojicha drink, this cafe won't disappoint you.

review_text: 🍵 Matcha: Ordered the Matcha Latte Vol. 2 and I'm obsessed! Earthy, bitter, and perfectly balanced. Unlike other cafés where I need to sub oat milk for the matcha flavor to stand out, this one delivered even with the default milk. The serving size was generous, and honestly, Steep Kohi in Davao serves better matcha than many places in Manila, a pleasant surprise! 🏠 Ambience: Japanese-inspired and cozy, best for takeout since seating is limited. Not study-friendly, but a great stop if you just want a really good latte. 👩 🍳 Service: Loved that they placed a sign about the 15–20 min wait time, transparent and helpful. Watching them make lattes in front was entertaining, so the wait didn't feel long. Hoping they expand soon with more space and staff. 💸 Value: Reasonable price for the quality and portion. Definitely worth it. ✨ Overall: By far the best matcha spot in the city. Will keep coming back!

They have outlets too, so it's a good place if you need to work or charge your devices. I've heard their pastas and sandwiches are worth trying, so I might come back for those next time. Overall, I really enjoyed my short stay, definitely a chill spot I'd visit again.

review_text: Went there December 16, 2025. Such a journey to come here. Using Buhangin-Roxas DCbus at 6:30pm and got to Citygate mall around 7:20pm, the walk to the cafe made me arrived at 7:45pm. Took the ₱240 8oz hot CLASSIC without signature ratio honey + first harvest matcha +oatside milk. Availed the reusable cup deal so minus -₱ 10. I had a great time standing and talking to the matcharista and the rest of the ates and kuyas are a vibe. Like they add to the homey ambience. Like the fact there was a door behind the matcharista. Got some logo stickers and a Tala cup. Finished 8:55pm then got to the DCbus stop at 9:10pm. It was a great thing that the driver stopped to eat. Otherwise, get there at 8:55pm. Got home and placed ice in the Matcha. Yah that what it looks like. Will come back next year. Happy holidays

I had high hopes for Martin Asian Cuisine after reading several positive reviews on other websites, but unfortunately, our experience fell short of expectations. The restaurant is tucked inside Bloom Cafe, which made it a bit tricky to locate at first. We visited on a Sunday lunchtime. The space was small but visually appealing, with natural light streaming in and a thoughtfully designed setup. There were only about five tables, all occupied at the time. Their menu offered a good variety of Asian dishes, which we were excited to try. There was only one waitress serving all customers, and while she was polite and upfront about the expected 30-minute wait time, our food ended up taking over an hour to be served. We only ordered three items: Tom Yum Goong, Goi Cuon, and a chicken dish. One thing to note: only sodas are available for drinks at Martin. If you want something else, you'll have to order separately at Bloom Cafe. We also encountered a minor hygiene issue. One of our bowls had a dead insect stuck to it. While the staff quickly replaced it without question, it did affect our overall impression of the kitchen's attention to cleanliness. As for the food: The Goi Cuon had an overcooked wrapper and oily vegetables, lacking the light and fresh profile we were expecting. The Tom Yum Goong had decent flavor, but it was served lukewarm and the shrimps were overcooked. The chicken dish was okay; similar to inasal with soy sauce. We paid ₱985 for the three dishes. They only accept cash or GCash, which might be inconvenient for some. On the positive side, they were able to provide a sales invoice, which we appreciated. The invoice had Bloom Cafe's name on the header, which further suggests the two businesses are connected. Overall, while the space itself is aesthetically pleasing and has potential, the long waiting time, inconsistent food quality, limited drink service, and minor hygiene concerns made the experience underwhelming. I hope improvements are made in both kitchen operations and customer communication.

They help you to find the right meal and drinks for you. At last the atmosphere. Inside it's cooled and clean. The same goes for the outside. The look is modern. It was undergoing some maintenance when I was there but I still could eat outside. Atmosphere only got 4 instead of 5 stars because it is right beside the main road. So it is very noisy. But apart from that I have nothing to complain. I'd definitely recommend this restaurant. King regards Peter

review_text: Had a nice experience at Bloom Coffee. ☕️ Their coffees are surprisingly good! Forgot) is good too, not sweet and delivers a long-lasting aftertaste. 🍴 I love their breakfast quesadilla! It was savory and the eggs in it are fluffy. 💵 Accepts cash/card 🌐 They have fast wifi. After you order, they give you a voucher you can use to access their wifi (max 4hrs) 👨 🍳 Our overall experience was good, but our order took almost 1 hour to arrive (and there wasn't even much people in the cafe). Although, It didn't create hassle for us because we were not hungry, nor in a hurry. ✍️Plenty of wall sockets. They have a functioning toilet. Has indoor and outdoor seating. Would definitely go back when in the area!

place_name: The Coffee Bar at GMall of Davao
review_text: Today me and friends decided to visit this new café in Gensan, The Coffee Bar, it was our first time and our experience was disappointing. First, the cashier S****** told us that the serving time of our orders, iced matcha latte and iced caramel latte will take 1 hour and 30 mins, we were confused why but we chose to understand so we did not really mind it. Second, the cashier was somewhat unprofessional for slamming my credit card and receipt. Third, my iced matcha latte had hair inside. Lastly, when I asked her before we left if she found any Uniqlo paper bag, she told me no but the other staff took the initiative to check if they had kept it. Luckily, it was given back to me and when she saw me with the paper bag, she simply ignored me. It is just disappointing how some staff treat young customers poorly compared to those that are older. For the food and drinks, it is far different from their Davao branch. I hope your service and food quality will improve.

place_name: The Crazy Bite Co. Sky Cafe
review_text: The Crazy Bite Co. Sky Cafe is one of those places in Davao that feels like it has its own personality. Every time I go there, it gives me this casual, late-night, comfort-food kind of vibe that makes it easy to just relax and enjoy the moment. It is also 24/7. The food serving focuses on big portions and satisfying meals that actually hit the spot when you are hungry. There were times I went there expecting just a quick bite, but ended up surprisingly full and satisfied. The atmosphere is also a big part of the experience. It has that laid-back café feel where you can either hang out with friends or just sit quietly while eating. On good days, it even feels a bit cozy, especially when it's not too crowded. It's the kind of place where time passes without you really noticing. Service-wise, sometimes they took a long time to give your order.

I wish they put up a sign where the exact entrance to the building is because I had some trouble looking for it (im not from Davao).

place_name: The Crazy Bite Co. Sky Cafe
review_text: After the first simbang gabi for 2024, I needed to get breakfast. Beshy Google was as usual helpful and gave me several recomm. Crazy Bite was listed as the second, which was weird as it was the nearest. Took a Grab ride since it was my first time. Didn't know where it actually was. The driver also didnt't know where it was. We asked an on-duty S.G. in the area where LHL Bldg was, and voila. You have to take an elevator ride to go up to the 5th floor of LHL Bldg. When you get off, you take 2 more flights of stairs to get to the 6th floor where they were located. I was in for a surprise with the staff's energetic and ''crazy' greetings. They do the same thing when you leave. I ordered chicken and a burger. Went to the 2nd level (there are 2 levels) where I waited to be buzzed for my order. I liked the 2nd level better than the 1st. You get some sights there. 👀 Nothing on the 1st level, but it was better there during that 1st visit. Here's the reason why. Two customers (friends) sat at the table beside me. They were loud with expletives to match. The other customers at the other tables (there were 3 other occupied tables) were not the loud, dirty-mouth types. These 2 were. So. I moved down to the 1st level. (I should've taken a photo of those two as a warning to you. LOL). The food? Nothing crazy about the chicken, but at least it was not bland and fried perfectly. It was the cheese burger I was crazy about. The flavor was really good and it was still pleasantly warm, given it was the second to be consumed. The staff? Let's get back to that energetic greeting. The same energy is evident in the way most of them talk to each other. Loud. 🥴 Like the person they were talking to was a mile away, but were not. Same energy in the way they serve you and speak with you: fast, clearly and with a smile. The photo of the tissue holder and the message board right on top of it tells its own story. My first visit was not totally a bad one, not totally a good one either. It's a tie? 🤪

review_text: The place was great and the staff were very nice and welcoming, the view from the top was amazing! You can see a large part of the city there. The lobby like part of the establishment has a backyard party vibe in it, which was a nice touch. Beside the horrendous use of stairs in my first visit (the elevator is probably fixed now), the food was delicious! Albeit expensive, the menu could use a bit more expansion like include some add ons with its price, addition of more menu items (I dont know which but it is a suggestion) and I did notice the VIP lounge, wondering if they advertise that area for use The place can cater a group of 6 i think, especially in the rooftop portion with a nice view. One note though, The nacho menu doesnt put the cheese, condiments and the meat spread throughout from the top to bottom, leaving the bottom part to be bland without the cheese and other stuff, in my visit the large nachos were on top and as you get down, the piece are smaller until it goes to crumbs Overall the place was very nice, clean, and I advice bringing a jacket when staying upstairs, sometimes it would get drafty

place_name: The Crazy Bite Co. Sky Cafe
review_text: The location is pretty nice, if you're looking for a cozy place to eat while enjoying the city view. Food servings are generous. Service crews are nice and welcoming. It's a decent place to eat and chill, the music is not too loud. The restrooms are clean. They only have limited tables and chairs so you might have to wait a few minutes before you can secure a table, the staff is also accommodating, they will seat you right away if there are customers waiting to dine. So far, it has been a good experience. Their poppers are delicious because they are made out of chicken breast meat, their iced choco is delicious (not sure if they call it iced choco as long as it's in the non-coffee section) I like it because it's not too sweet and chocolatey, it's not like an instant choco drink. Their meal set B (2nd photo) is good for 2, you can order additional rice if you like rice ☺️. A few burgers are filling, the patty is big (I'm not a fan of the taste & texture) but maybe your taste buds will like it 😉

review_text: The Cafe offers a unique ambiance that combines a cozy atmosphere with a beautiful indoor garden setup. It has homey decor and a calm ambiance that makes visitors feel relaxed and at ease with picturesque indoor garden with plants and quirky trinkets, making every corner Instagram-worthy. I have not asked but I guess some of the merchandise here are a local art made by the owner or owner's personal selection. Also, due to limited seating, the cafe has an intimate setting, but reservations are recommended to secure a spot. The ambiance is complemented by their tasty food and drinks, including coffee, tea, sandwiches, pasta, and pastries. And as I see their menu, they really put efforts into carving their crafts. The drinks we ordered were well-made with a rich, full-bodied flavor, though for me and my friends, it was a bit too weak, so a stronger brew might suit better. Overall, The Secret Garden Cafe provides a charming and peaceful ambiance, perfect for those looking to unwind and enjoy good food and company.

review_text: The Secret Garden Cafe lives up to its name. It's a hidden gem in a residential subdivision that offers some lovely coffee, pasta, and one of the best grilled cheese sandwiches I've had so far. The place is quaint and has a few seating but it's not crowded. The ambience is very nice, green and cozy. They have a lot of well curated pieces that make the Cafe both look like a garden and an artist's haven. Prices are also reasonable for the good quality of food and drinks they offer. My only issue would be the parking. If you don't mind walking, you can drop your car by savemore but I wouldn't recommend it in the evening as the street can be quite dim. Overall, I'm impressed and will definitely come back more often.

review_text: Finally another breakfast joint for Davao! I give everything a 10/10! The place is not hard to find and with plenty of parking space. We ordered TYS pancakes (classic pancakes), chicken & waffles, chicken tocino, bangus, Hojicha and TYS latte. Pancakes - soft, fluffy and tastes like bananas. Buttercream on the side is a good addition if you don't like syrup. Chicken & Waffles - chicken so crispy yet moist, seasoned nicely. Mochi waffles soft and not dry. They have a black sesame butter which is very good and have to try. Chicken tocino - made like a rice bowl is also good try because the chicken pieces used were tender with less fat making it a healthy meal. On the side they have 2 eggs of your choice of sunny side up or scrambled. Bangus - includes 2 pieces of baby Bangus with were crispy and good to pair with eggs. Hojicha - served hot or iced, we got hot. Served a little sweet but still good! TYS Latte - very creamy but not sweet, served iced which is a good drink for a hot day

It is what bibingka should be, matambok, except without the cracks. HAHAHAHA. It is also what pancakes should be, fluffy! The toppings are bursting with flavor and texture. review_text: I am writing this review directly from the venue to express my deep disappointment with the service at Yukiss Cafe & Events Room. We arrived at exactly 10:00 PM. The doorman/guard (the guy wearing a red-striped shirt) was very polite and greeted us well. However, the energy completely shifted once we stepped inside. There were three staff members at the counter: a young man and two women, one of whom was older. They all had frowns on their faces, looking completely unhappy to see customers. They initially handed us the menu, but just as we were about to order, they abruptly informed us that they were already closing. We pointed out that according to Google and Facebook, their operating hours are until 1:00 AM. However, they told us that they actually close at 11:40 PM. I politely asked the older woman for an explanation regarding this discrepancy, asking, "Ano masasabi mo, ma'am?" (What can you say about this, ma'am?). She completely ignored me and gave no response. Despite saying they were closing, they still let us order. Since we traveled all the way here—and the location is quite hidden, dark to get into, and exhausting to reach—we didn't want our effort to go to waste. We originally planned to sing videoke and order ramen, but our mood was completely ruined. We ended up just ordering 4 Smirnoff Mules because of the pressure that they were closing, even though we could still hear other customers singing videoke. To make matters worse, the older woman audibly remarked, "Nag sayo unta mo" (You should have come earlier). It felt like a joke because they were making it seem like it was our fault, which was shocking. Less than two drinks in—not even halfway through our beverages—they immediately demanded payment because they needed to do a "cash count." There was absolutely no consideration for the customers. When we left, there was no "thank you" or even a simple "pasensya po" (we're sorry) from that older woman. As someone who understands the food industry, I completely get that they were exhausted and wanted to go home. I know how hard the job is, and I would have gladly understood if they just handled us properly. In fact, I kept smiling and even made light jokes to keep things light. I handled myself nicely, but the treatment I got in return was just rude. What hurts the most is that I brought my family with me. To have my family go through such a terrible and unwelcoming experience really hurts on my part. The way they practically shooed us away proved they have zero knowledge of customer service. The staff badly needs a seminar on hospitality and how to speak politely to paying customers. To be fair, the doorman in the red stripes was courteous. The young male staff member, who was clearly forced by the two women to collect our payment early, was also polite to us. Meanwhile, the two female staff members hid and ducked behind the counter out of embarrassment. The embarrassment is real. The place itself is beautiful, well-designed, and aesthetic. It is clear that the owner invested a lot of thought, money, and effort into the decorations and details. It's such a pity that a great business is being ruined by the terrible attitude of its employees. Looking at other Google reviews, it seems I am not alone—most complaints are about the staff. I truly feel bad for the owner if they are unaware of how their employees are sabotaging their investment. Pros: Beautiful aesthetic, polite doorman, and polite young male staff. Cons: Horrible customer service from the female staff, inconsistent operating hours, and very rude, dismissive behavior towards families.

place_name: The Matcha Tokyo - Azuela High Street
review_text: April 2026 – Located at Cluster 1, Unit 2 of Azuela High Street in Lanang, The Matcha Tokyo is one of the first establishments to open in this new complex. It is easy to find, as it fronts the courtyard and the Eco-bike station, right near the Azuela High Street signage. First, be prepared for the price point as this is an expensive spot. Aesthetically, the store is stunning; it's bathed in a clean stucco finish with beautiful wooden furniture and a sleek, curved cushioned bench that spans the length of the space. Form the menu, we ordered the Matcha Frozen Latte (₱280), Ube Matcha Latte (₱280), and Matcha Frozen Lemonade (₱205). While we are no strangers to matcha, we were genuinely surprised by the lack of balance in these drinks. Matcha Frozen Lemonade. This was the only drink we enjoyed, though primarily for the lemonade itself; the matcha felt more like a thematic garnish than a core flavor. Ube Matcha Latte. This was a total disappointment. It lacked any semblance of Ube – the iconic Philippine purple yam now famous worldwide, thanks to Jollibee. Instead, the drink was overwhelmingly bitter, reminiscent of blended ampalaya (bitter gourd). Matcha Frozen Latte. Unfortunately, the flavor profile was completely off. I understand the appeal of high-quality matcha, but this mixture was unpalatable. We struggled to understand the high 4.7-star rating. Perhaps we ordered the wrong items, but it was a disappointing nightcap. I noticed the store offers stickers to those who leave reviews; however, I prefer to provide an honest account of our experience. Additionally, the cleanliness left much to be desired. We sat at our table for quite some time while waiting for our drinks but used items from previous customers remained uncleaned the entire time. For a premium-priced establishment, the service and quality should be much higher. Overall, not the best matcha experience, and if this is the standard, maybe, we are not made for matcha.
